<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api">The Confluence Cloud REST API v1.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

This document describes the REST API and resources provided by Confluence. The REST APIs are for developers who want to integrate Confluence into their application and for administrators who want to script interactions with the Confluence server.Confluence's REST APIs provide access to resources (data entities) via URI paths. To use a REST API, your application will make an HTTP request and parse the response. The response format is JSON. Your methods will be the standard HTTP methods like GET, PUT, POST and DELETE. Because the REST API is based on open standards, you can use any web development language to access the API.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://developer.atlassian.com//your-domain.atlassian.net">https://developer.atlassian.com//your-domain.atlassian.net</a>

<a href="https://atlassian.com/terms/">Terms of service</a>

<a href="https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/">The online and complete version of the Confluence Cloud REST API docs.</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic You can access this resource via basic auth.

- oAuth2 authentication. This API uses OAuth 2 with the authorizationCode grant flow.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize](https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token](https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token)

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-audit">Audit</h1>

## Get audit records

<a id="opIdgetAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/audit \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/audit`

Returns all records in the audit log, optionally for a certain date range.
This contains information about events like space exports, group membership
changes, app installations, etc. For more information, see
[Audit log](https://confluence.atlassian.com/confcloud/audit-log-802164269.html)
in the Confluence administrator's guide.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

<h3 id="get-audit-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startDate|query|string|false|Filters the results to the records on or after the `startDate`.<br>The `startDate` must be specified as [epoch time](https://www.epochconverter.com/) in milliseconds.|
|endDate|query|string|false|Filters the results to the records on or before the `endDate`.<br>The `endDate` must be specified as [epoch time](https://www.epochconverter.com/) in milliseconds.|
|searchString|query|string|false|Filters the results to records that have string property values<br>matching the `searchString`.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned records.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of records to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "author": {
        "type": "user",
        "displayName": "string",
        "operations": [
          {
            "operation": "administer",
            "targetType": "string"
          }
        ],
        "username": "string",
        "userKey": "string",
        "accountId": "string",
        "accountType": "string",
        "externalCollaborator": true,
        "isExternalCollaborator": true,
        "isGuest": true,
        "publicName": "string"
      },
      "remoteAddress": "string",
      "creationDate": 0,
      "summary": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "category": "string",
      "sysAdmin": true,
      "superAdmin": true,
      "affectedObject": {
        "name": "string",
        "objectType": "string"
      },
      "changedValues": [
        {
          "name": "string",
          "oldValue": "string",
          "hiddenOldValue": "string",
          "newValue": "string",
          "hiddenNewValue": "string"
        }
      ],
      "associatedObjects": [
        {
          "name": "string",
          "objectType": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-audit-records-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested records are returned.|[AuditRecordArray](#schemaauditrecordarray)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to view the audit<br>log.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:audit-log:confluence )
</aside>

## Create audit record

<a id="opIdcreateAuditRecord"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/audit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "author": {
      "type": "user",
      "displayName": "string",
      "operations": [
        {
          "operation": "administer",
          "targetType": "string"
        }
      ],
      "username": "string",
      "userKey": "string"
    },
    "remoteAddress": "string",
    "creationDate": 0,
    "summary": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "category": "string",
    "sysAdmin": false,
    "affectedObject": {
      "name": "string",
      "objectType": "string"
    },
    "changedValues": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "oldValue": "string",
        "hiddenOldValue": "string",
        "newValue": "string",
        "hiddenNewValue": "string"
      }
    ],
    "associatedObjects": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "objectType": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/audit`

Creates a record in the audit log.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "author": {
    "type": "user",
    "displayName": "string",
    "operations": [
      {
        "operation": "administer",
        "targetType": "string"
      }
    ],
    "username": "string",
    "userKey": "string"
  },
  "remoteAddress": "string",
  "creationDate": 0,
  "summary": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "category": "string",
  "sysAdmin": false,
  "affectedObject": {
    "name": "string",
    "objectType": "string"
  },
  "changedValues": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "oldValue": "string",
      "hiddenOldValue": "string",
      "newValue": "string",
      "hiddenNewValue": "string"
    }
  ],
  "associatedObjects": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "objectType": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-audit-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AuditRecordCreate](#schemaauditrecordcreate)|true|The record to be created in the audit log.|
|» author|body|object|false|The user that actioned the event. If `author` is not specified, then all<br>`author` properties will be set to null/empty, except for `type` which<br>will be set to 'user'.|
|» » type|body|string|true|Set to 'user'.|
|» » displayName|body|string|false|The name that is displayed on the audit log in the Confluence UI.|
|» » operations|body|[[OperationCheckResult](#schemaoperationcheckresult)]|false|Always defaults to null.|
|» » username|body|[GenericUserName](#schemagenericusername)|false|This property is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|» » userKey|body|[GenericUserKey](#schemagenericuserkey)|false|This property is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|» remoteAddress|body|string|true|The IP address of the computer where the event was initiated from.|
|» creationDate|body|integer(int64)|false|The creation date-time of the audit record, as a timestamp. This is converted<br>to a date-time display in the Confluence UI. If the `creationDate` is not<br>specified, then it will be set to the timestamp for the current date-time.|
|» summary|body|string|false|The summary of the event, which is displayed in the 'Change' column on<br>the audit log in the Confluence UI.|
|» description|body|string|false|A long description of the event, which is displayed in the 'Description'<br>field on the audit log in the Confluence UI.|
|» category|body|string|false|The category of the event, which is displayed in the 'Event type' column<br>on the audit log in the Confluence UI.|
|» sysAdmin|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the event was actioned by a system administrator.|
|» affectedObject|body|[AffectedObject](#schemaaffectedobject)|false|none|
|» changedValues|body|[[ChangedValue](#schemachangedvalue)]|false|The values that were changed in the event.|
|» associatedObjects|body|[[AffectedObject](#schemaaffectedobject)]|false|Objects that were associated with the event. For example, if the event<br>was a space permission change then the associated object would be the<br>space.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|user|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "author": {
    "type": "user",
    "displayName": "string",
    "operations": [
      {
        "operation": "administer",
        "targetType": "string"
      }
    ],
    "username": "string",
    "userKey": "string",
    "accountId": "string",
    "accountType": "string",
    "externalCollaborator": true,
    "isExternalCollaborator": true,
    "isGuest": true,
    "publicName": "string"
  },
  "remoteAddress": "string",
  "creationDate": 0,
  "summary": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "category": "string",
  "sysAdmin": true,
  "superAdmin": true,
  "affectedObject": {
    "name": "string",
    "objectType": "string"
  },
  "changedValues": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "oldValue": "string",
      "hiddenOldValue": "string",
      "newValue": "string",
      "hiddenNewValue": "string"
    }
  ],
  "associatedObjects": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "objectType": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-audit-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the record is created in the audit log.|[AuditRecord](#schemaauditrecord)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the `remoteAddress` property is not specified.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:audit-log:confluence write:audit-log:confluence )
</aside>

## Export audit records

<a id="opIdexportAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/audit/export \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/audit/export`

Exports audit records as a CSV file or ZIP file.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

<h3 id="export-audit-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startDate|query|string|false|Filters the exported results to the records on or after the `startDate`.<br>The `startDate` must be specified as [epoch time](https://www.epochconverter.com/) in milliseconds.|
|endDate|query|string|false|Filters the exported results to the records on or before the `endDate`.<br>The `endDate` must be specified as [epoch time](https://www.epochconverter.com/) in milliseconds.|
|searchString|query|string|false|Filters the exported results to records that have string property values<br>matching the `searchString`.|
|format|query|string|false|The format of the export file for the audit records.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|csv|
|format|zip|

<h3 id="export-audit-records-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested export of the audit records is returned.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to view the audit<br>log.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:audit-log:confluence )
</aside>

## Get retention period

<a id="opIdgetRetentionPeriod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/audit/retention \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/audit/retention`

Returns the retention period for records in the audit log. The retention
period is how long an audit record is kept for, from creation date until
it is deleted.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "number": 0,
  "units": "NANOS"
}
```

<h3 id="get-retention-period-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested retention period is returned.|[RetentionPeriod](#schemaretentionperiod)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to view the audit<br>log.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:audit-log:confluence )
</aside>

## Set retention period

<a id="opIdsetRetentionPeriod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/audit/retention \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "number": 0,
    "units": "NANOS"
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/audit/retention`

Sets the retention period for records in the audit log. The retention period
can be set to a maximum of 1 year.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "number": 0,
  "units": "NANOS"
}
```

<h3 id="set-retention-period-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RetentionPeriod](#schemaretentionperiod)|true|The updated retention period.|
|» number|body|integer(int32)|true|The number of units for the retention period.|
|» units|body|string|true|The unit of time that the retention period is measured in.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» units|NANOS|
|» units|MICROS|
|» units|MILLIS|
|» units|SECONDS|
|» units|MINUTES|
|» units|HOURS|
|» units|HALF_DAYS|
|» units|DAYS|
|» units|WEEKS|
|» units|MONTHS|
|» units|YEARS|
|» units|DECADES|
|» units|CENTURIES|
|» units|MILLENNIA|
|» units|ERAS|
|» units|FOREVER|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "number": 0,
  "units": "NANOS"
}
```

<h3 id="set-retention-period-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the retention period is updated.|[RetentionPeriod](#schemaretentionperiod)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to view the audit<br>log.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:audit-log:confluence )
</aside>

## Get audit records for time period

<a id="opIdgetAuditRecordsForTimePeriod"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/audit/since \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/audit/since`

Returns records from the audit log, for a time period back from the current
date. For example, you can use this method to get the last 3 months of records.

This contains information about events like space exports, group membership
changes, app installations, etc. For more information, see
[Audit log](https://confluence.atlassian.com/confcloud/audit-log-802164269.html)
in the Confluence administrator's guide.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

|number|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of units for the time period.|
|units|query|string|false|The unit of time that the time period is measured in.|
|searchString|query|string|false|Filters the results to records that have string property values<br>matching the `searchString`.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned records.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of records to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

|units|CENTURIES|

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-analytics">Analytics</h1>

## Get views

<a id="opIdgetViews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/analytics/content/string/views \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/analytics/content/{contentId}/views`

Get the total number of views a piece of content has.

<h3 id="get-views-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentId|path|string|true|The ID of the content to get the views for.|
|fromDate|query|string|false|The number of views for the content since the date.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "count": 0
}
```

<h3 id="get-views-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the total number of views for the content.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if client input is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the authentication credentials are missing<br>from the request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br>- There is no content with the given ID.|None|

<h3 id="get-views-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|The content ID.|
|count|integer|false|none|The total number of views for the content.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Get viewers

<a id="opIdgetViewers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/analytics/content/string/viewers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/analytics/content/{contentId}/viewers`

Get the total number of distinct viewers a piece of content has.

<h3 id="get-viewers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentId|path|string|true|The ID of the content to get the viewers for.|
|fromDate|query|string|false|The number of views for the content since the date.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "count": 0
}
```

<h3 id="get-viewers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the total number of distinct viewers for the content.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if client input is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the authentication credentials are missing<br>from the request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br>- There is no content with the given ID.|None|

<h3 id="get-viewers-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|The content ID.|
|count|integer|false|none|The total number of distinct viewers for the content.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content">Content</h1>

## Archive pages

<a id="opIdarchivePages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/archive \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "pages": [
      {
        "id": 0
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/archive`

Archives a list of pages. The pages to be archived are specified as a list of content IDs.
This API accepts the archival request and returns a task ID.
The archival process happens asynchronously.
Use the /longtask/<taskId> REST API to get the copy task status.

Each content ID needs to resolve to page objects that are not already in an archived state.
The content IDs need not belong to the same space.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Archive' permission for each of the pages in the corresponding space it belongs to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pages": [
    {
      "id": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="archive-pages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|The pages to be archived.|
|» pages|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » id|body|integer(int64)|true|The `id` of the page to be archived.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "ari": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "links": {
    "status": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="archive-pages-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Returned if the archive request has been submitted.|[LongTask](#schemalongtask)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br>- there is an archival job already running for the tenant.<br>- the number of pages to archive is larger than the limit of 300.<br>- any of the content IDs specified in the array do not resolve to pages.<br>- any of the specified pages are already archived.<br>- the request is coming from a free edition tenant.<br>- the request is coming from a non premium edition tenant with more than 1 page ID<br>  in the archive request.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Publish shared draft

<a id="opIdpublishSharedDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/blueprint/instance/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "version": {
      "number": 0
    },
    "title": "string",
    "type": "page",
    "status": "current",
    "space": {
      "key": "string"
    },
    "ancestors": [
      {
        "id": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/content/blueprint/instance/{draftId}`

Publishes a shared draft of a page created from a blueprint.

By default, the following objects are expanded: `body.storage`, `history`, `space`, `version`, `ancestors`.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the draft and 'Add' permission for the space that
the content will be created in.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "version": {
    "number": 0
  },
  "title": "string",
  "type": "page",
  "status": "current",
  "space": {
    "key": "string"
  },
  "ancestors": [
    {
      "id": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="publish-shared-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|draftId|path|string|true|The ID of the draft page that was created from a blueprint.<br>You can find the `draftId` in the Confluence application by<br>opening the draft page and checking the page URL.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the content to be updated, i.e. the draft. This is set<br>to 'draft' by default, so you shouldn't need to specify it.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand.<br><br>- `childTypes.all` returns whether the content has attachments, comments, or child pages/whiteboards.<br>Use this if you only need to check whether the content has children of a particular type.<br>- `childTypes.attachment` returns whether the content has attachments.<br>- `childTypes.comment` returns whether the content has comments.<br>- `childTypes.page` returns whether the content has child pages.<br>- `childTypes.whiteboard` returns whether the content has child whiteboards.<br>- `childTypes.database` returns whether the content has child databases.<br>- `childTypes.embed` returns whether the content has child embeds (smartlinks).<br>- `childTypes.folder` returns whether the content has child folders.<br>- `container` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information<br>returned by [Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br>- `metadata.currentuser` returns information about the current user in relation to the content,<br>including when they last viewed it, modified it, contributed to it, or added it as a favorite.<br>- `metadata.properties` returns content properties that have been set via the Confluence REST API.<br>- `metadata.labels` returns the labels that have been added to the content.<br>- `metadata.frontend` this property is only used by Atlassian.<br>- `operations` returns the operations for the content, which are used when setting permissions.<br>- `children.page` returns pages that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.database` returns databases that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.folder` returns folders that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.attachment` returns all attachments for the content.<br>- `children.comment` returns all comments on the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to read the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to read the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups, because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to update the content.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to update the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `history` returns the history of the content, including the date it was created.<br>- `history.lastUpdated` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including<br>who updated it and when it was updated.<br>- `history.previousVersion` returns information about the update prior to the current content update.<br>- `history.contributors` returns all of the users who have contributed to the content.<br>- `history.nextVersion` returns information about the update after to the current content update.<br>- `ancestors` returns the parent content, if the content is a page or whiteboard.<br>- `body` returns the body of the content in different formats, including the editor format,<br>view format, and export format.<br>- `body.storage` returns the body of content in storage format.<br>- `body.view` returns the body of content in view format.<br>- `version` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including who updated it<br>and when it was updated.<br>- `descendants.page` returns pages that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.database` returns databases that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.folder` returns folders that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.attachment` returns all attachments for the content, same as `children.attachment`.<br>- `descendants.comment` returns all comments on the content, same as `children.comment`.<br>- `space` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information returned by<br>[Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br><br>In addition, the following comment-specific expansions can be used:<br>- `extensions.inlineProperties` returns inline comment-specific properties.<br>- `extensions.resolution` returns the resolution status of each comment.|
|body|body|[ContentBlueprintDraft](#schemacontentblueprintdraft)|true|none|
|» version|body|object|true|The version for the new content.|
|» » number|body|integer(int32)|true|The version number. Set this to `1`.|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the content. If you don't want to change the title,<br>set this to the current title of the draft.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of content. Set this to `page`.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the content. Set this to `current` or omit it altogether.|
|» space|body|object|false|The space for the content.|
|» » key|body|string(int32)|true|The key of the space|
|» ancestors|body|[object]|false|The new ancestor (i.e. parent page) for the content. If you have<br>specified an ancestor, you must also specify a `space` property<br>in the request body for the space that the ancestor is in.<br><br>Note, if you specify more than one ancestor, the last ID in the array<br>will be selected as the parent page for the content.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The content ID of the ancestor.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|page|
|» status|current|

<h3 id="publish-shared-draft-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the draft was successfully published.|[Content](#schemacontent)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if a title is not specified or a page with the<br>title already exists.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the version is not set to 1.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Publish legacy draft

<a id="opIdpublishLegacyDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/blueprint/instance/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "version": {
      "number": 0
    },
    "title": "string",
    "type": "page",
    "status": "current",
    "space": {
      "key": "string"
    },
    "ancestors": [
      {
        "id": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/blueprint/instance/{draftId}`

Publishes a legacy draft of a page created from a blueprint. Legacy drafts
will eventually be removed in favor of shared drafts. For now, this method
works the same as [Publish shared draft](#api-content-blueprint-instance-draftId-put).

By default, the following objects are expanded: `body.storage`, `history`, `space`, `version`, `ancestors`.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the draft and 'Add' permission for the space that
the content will be created in.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "version": {
    "number": 0
  },
  "title": "string",
  "type": "page",
  "status": "current",
  "space": {
    "key": "string"
  },
  "ancestors": [
    {
      "id": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="publish-legacy-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|draftId|path|string|true|The ID of the draft page that was created from a blueprint.<br>You can find the `draftId` in the Confluence application by<br>opening the draft page and checking the page URL.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the content to be updated, i.e. the draft. This is set<br>to 'draft' by default, so you shouldn't need to specify it.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand.<br><br>- `childTypes.all` returns whether the content has attachments, comments, or child pages/whiteboards.<br>Use this if you only need to check whether the content has children of a particular type.<br>- `childTypes.attachment` returns whether the content has attachments.<br>- `childTypes.comment` returns whether the content has comments.<br>- `childTypes.page` returns whether the content has child pages.<br>- `childTypes.whiteboard` returns whether the content has child whiteboards.<br>- `childTypes.database` returns whether the content has child databases.<br>- `childTypes.embed` returns whether the content has child embeds (smartlinks).<br>- `childTypes.folder` returns whether the content has child folders.<br>- `container` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information<br>returned by [Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br>- `metadata.currentuser` returns information about the current user in relation to the content,<br>including when they last viewed it, modified it, contributed to it, or added it as a favorite.<br>- `metadata.properties` returns content properties that have been set via the Confluence REST API.<br>- `metadata.labels` returns the labels that have been added to the content.<br>- `metadata.frontend` this property is only used by Atlassian.<br>- `operations` returns the operations for the content, which are used when setting permissions.<br>- `children.page` returns pages that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.database` returns databases that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.folder` returns folders that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.attachment` returns all attachments for the content.<br>- `children.comment` returns all comments on the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to read the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to read the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups, because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to update the content.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to update the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `history` returns the history of the content, including the date it was created.<br>- `history.lastUpdated` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including<br>who updated it and when it was updated.<br>- `history.previousVersion` returns information about the update prior to the current content update.<br>- `history.contributors` returns all of the users who have contributed to the content.<br>- `history.nextVersion` returns information about the update after to the current content update.<br>- `ancestors` returns the parent content, if the content is a page or whiteboard.<br>- `body` returns the body of the content in different formats, including the editor format,<br>view format, and export format.<br>- `body.storage` returns the body of content in storage format.<br>- `body.view` returns the body of content in view format.<br>- `version` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including who updated it<br>and when it was updated.<br>- `descendants.page` returns pages that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.database` returns databases that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.folder` returns folders that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.attachment` returns all attachments for the content, same as `children.attachment`.<br>- `descendants.comment` returns all comments on the content, same as `children.comment`.<br>- `space` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information returned by<br>[Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br><br>In addition, the following comment-specific expansions can be used:<br>- `extensions.inlineProperties` returns inline comment-specific properties.<br>- `extensions.resolution` returns the resolution status of each comment.|
|body|body|[ContentBlueprintDraft](#schemacontentblueprintdraft)|true|none|
|» version|body|object|true|The version for the new content.|
|» » number|body|integer(int32)|true|The version number. Set this to `1`.|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the content. If you don't want to change the title,<br>set this to the current title of the draft.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of content. Set this to `page`.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the content. Set this to `current` or omit it altogether.|
|» space|body|object|false|The space for the content.|
|» » key|body|string(int32)|true|The key of the space|
|» ancestors|body|[object]|false|The new ancestor (i.e. parent page) for the content. If you have<br>specified an ancestor, you must also specify a `space` property<br>in the request body for the space that the ancestor is in.<br><br>Note, if you specify more than one ancestor, the last ID in the array<br>will be selected as the parent page for the content.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The content ID of the ancestor.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|page|
|» status|current|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Search content by CQL

<a id="opIdsearchContentByCQL"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/search?cql=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/search`

Returns the list of content that matches a Confluence Query Language
(CQL) query. For information on CQL, see:
[Advanced searching using CQL](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/advanced-searching-using-cql/).

Example initial call:
```
/wiki/rest/api/content/search?cql=type=page&limit=25
```

Example response:
```
{
  "results": [
    { ... },
    { ... },
    ...
    { ... }
  ],
  "limit": 25,
  "size": 25,
  ...
  "_links": {
    "base": "<url>",
    "context": "<url>",
    "next": "/rest/api/content/search?cql=type=page&limit=25&cursor=raNDoMsTRiNg",
    "self": "<url>"
  }
}
```

When additional results are available, returns `next` and `prev` URLs to retrieve them in subsequent calls. The URLs each contain a cursor that points to the appropriate set of results. Use `limit` to specify the number of results returned in each call.
Example subsequent call (taken from example response):
```
/wiki/rest/api/content/search?cql=type=page&limit=25&cursor=raNDoMsTRiNg
```
The response to this will have a `prev` URL similar to the `next` in the example response.

If the expand query parameter is used with the `body.export_view` and/or `body.styled_view` properties, then the query limit parameter will be restricted to a maximum value of 25.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).
Only content that the user has permission to view will be returned.

<h3 id="search-content-by-cql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cql|query|string|true|The CQL string that is used to find the requested content.|
|cqlcontext|query|string|false|The space, content, and content status to execute the search against.<br>Specify this as an object with the following properties:<br><br>- `spaceKey` Key of the space to search against. Optional.<br>- `contentId` ID of the content to search against. Optional. Must<br>be in the space spacified by `spaceKey`.<br>- `contentStatuses` Content statuses to search against. Optional.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand.<br><br>- `childTypes.all` returns whether the content has attachments, comments, or child pages/whiteboards.<br>Use this if you only need to check whether the content has children of a particular type.<br>- `childTypes.attachment` returns whether the content has attachments.<br>- `childTypes.comment` returns whether the content has comments.<br>- `childTypes.page` returns whether the content has child pages.<br>- `childTypes.whiteboard` returns whether the content has child whiteboards.<br>- `childTypes.database` returns whether the content has child databases.<br>- `childTypes.embed` returns whether the content has child embeds (smartlinks).<br>- `childTypes.folder` returns whether the content has child folders.<br>- `container` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information<br>returned by [Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br>- `metadata.currentuser` returns information about the current user in relation to the content,<br>including when they last viewed it, modified it, contributed to it, or added it as a favorite.<br>- `metadata.properties` returns content properties that have been set via the Confluence REST API.<br>- `metadata.labels` returns the labels that have been added to the content.<br>- `metadata.frontend` this property is only used by Atlassian.<br>- `operations` returns the operations for the content, which are used when setting permissions.<br>- `children.page` returns pages that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.database` returns databases that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.folder` returns folders that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.attachment` returns all attachments for the content.<br>- `children.comment` returns all comments on the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to read the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to read the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups, because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to update the content.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to update the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `history` returns the history of the content, including the date it was created.<br>- `history.lastUpdated` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including<br>who updated it and when it was updated.<br>- `history.previousVersion` returns information about the update prior to the current content update.<br>- `history.contributors` returns all of the users who have contributed to the content.<br>- `history.nextVersion` returns information about the update after to the current content update.<br>- `ancestors` returns the parent content, if the content is a page or whiteboard.<br>- `body` returns the body of the content in different formats, including the editor format,<br>view format, and export format.<br>- `body.storage` returns the body of content in storage format.<br>- `body.view` returns the body of content in view format.<br>- `version` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including who updated it<br>and when it was updated.<br>- `descendants.page` returns pages that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.database` returns databases that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.folder` returns folders that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.attachment` returns all attachments for the content, same as `children.attachment`.<br>- `descendants.comment` returns all comments on the content, same as `children.comment`.<br>- `space` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information returned by<br>[Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br><br>In addition, the following comment-specific expansions can be used:<br>- `extensions.inlineProperties` returns inline comment-specific properties.<br>- `extensions.resolution` returns the resolution status of each comment.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Pointer to a set of search results, returned as part of the `next` or `prev` URL from the previous search call.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of content objects to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {}
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="search-content-by-cql-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested list of content is returned.|[ContentArray](#schemacontentarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the CQL is invalid or missing.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: search:confluence )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content---attachments">Content - attachments</h1>

## Create or update attachment

<a id="opIdcreateOrUpdateAttachments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/child/attachment \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'comment=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'minorEdit=@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment`

Adds an attachment to a piece of content. If the attachment already exists
for the content, then the attachment is updated (i.e. a new version of the
attachment is created).

Note, you must set a `X-Atlassian-Token: nocheck` header on the request
for this method, otherwise it will be blocked. This protects against XSRF
attacks, which is necessary as this method accepts multipart/form-data.

The media type 'multipart/form-data' is defined in [RFC 7578](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7578.txt).
Most client libraries have classes that make it easier to implement
multipart posts, like the [MultipartEntityBuilder](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-client-5.1.x/current/httpclient5/apidocs/)
Java class provided by Apache HTTP Components.

Note, according to [RFC 7578](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7578#section-4.5),
in the case where the form data is text,
the charset parameter for the "text/plain" Content-Type may be used to
indicate the character encoding used in that part. In the case of this
API endpoint, the `comment` body parameter should be sent with `type=text/plain`
and `charset=utf-8` values. This will force the charset to be UTF-8.

Example: This curl command attaches a file ('example.txt') to a piece of
content (id='123') with a comment and `minorEdits`=true. If the 'example.txt'
file already exists, it will update it with a new version of the attachment.

``` bash
curl -D- \
  -u admin:admin \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'X-Atlassian-Token: nocheck' \
  -F 'file=@"example.txt"' \
  -F 'minorEdit="true"' \
  -F 'comment="Example attachment comment"; type=text/plain; charset=utf-8' \
  http://myhost/rest/api/content/123/child/attachment
```
**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
comment: string
minorEdit: string
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content to add the attachment to.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the content that the attachment is being added to.<br>This should always be set to 'current'.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The relative location and name of the attachment to be added to<br>the content.|
|» comment|body|string(binary)|false|The comment for the attachment that is being added.<br>If you specify a comment, then every file must have a comment and<br>the comments must be in the same order as the files. Alternatively,<br>don't specify any comments.|
|» minorEdit|body|string(binary)|true|If `minorEdits` is set to 'true', no notification email or activity stream<br>will be generated when the attachment is added to the content.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|current|
|status|draft|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {}
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-attachment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the attachments were added to the content.|[ContentArray](#schemacontentarray)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- Attachments are disabled.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to add attachments to the<br>content.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- The requested content is not found.<br>- The user does not have permission to view it.<br>- The attachment exceeds the maximum configured attachment size.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-file )
</aside>

## Create attachment

<a id="opIdcreateAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/child/attachment \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'comment=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'minorEdit=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment`

Adds an attachment to a piece of content. This method only adds a new
attachment. If you want to update an existing attachment, use
[Create or update attachments](#api-content-id-child-attachment-put).

Note, you must set a `X-Atlassian-Token: nocheck` header on the request
for this method, otherwise it will be blocked. This protects against XSRF
attacks, which is necessary as this method accepts multipart/form-data.

The media type 'multipart/form-data' is defined in [RFC 7578](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7578.txt).
Most client libraries have classes that make it easier to implement
multipart posts, like the [MultipartEntityBuilder](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-client-5.1.x/current/httpclient5/apidocs/)
Java class provided by Apache HTTP Components.

Note, according to [RFC 7578](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7578#section-4.5),
in the case where the form data is text,
the charset parameter for the "text/plain" Content-Type may be used to
indicate the character encoding used in that part. In the case of this
API endpoint, the `comment` body parameter should be sent with `type=text/plain`
and `charset=utf-8` values. This will force the charset to be UTF-8.

Example: This curl command attaches a file ('example.txt') to a container
(id='123') with a comment and `minorEdits`=true.

``` bash
curl -D- \
  -u admin:admin \
  -X POST \
  -H 'X-Atlassian-Token: nocheck' \
  -F 'file=@"example.txt"' \
  -F 'minorEdit="true"' \
  -F 'comment="Example attachment comment"; type=text/plain; charset=utf-8' \
  https://myhost/wiki/rest/api/content/123/child/attachment
```
**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
comment: string
minorEdit: string
```

<h3 id="create-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content to add the attachment to.|
|status|query|string|false|The status of the content that the attachment is being added to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The relative location and name of the attachment to be added to<br>the content.|
|» comment|body|string(binary)|false|The comment for the attachment that is being added.<br>If you specify a comment, then every file must have a comment and<br>the comments must be in the same order as the files. Alternatively,<br>don't specify any comments.|
|» minorEdit|body|string(binary)|true|If `minorEdits` is set to 'true', no notification email or activity stream<br>will be generated when the attachment is added to the content.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|current|
|status|draft|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {}
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-attachment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the attachments were added to the content.|[ContentArray](#schemacontentarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the content already has an attachment with the same filename.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- Attachments are disabled in Confluence.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to add attachments to the<br>content.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- The requested content is not found.<br>- The user does not have permission to view it<br>- The attachment exceeds the maximum configured attachment size.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-file )
</aside>

## Update attachment properties

<a id="opIdupdateAttachmentProperties"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/child/attachment/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "status": "string",
    "title": "string",
    "container": {},
    "metadata": {
      "mediaType": "string"
    },
    "extensions": {},
    "version": {
      "by": {},
      "when": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "friendlyWhen": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "number": 0,
      "minorEdit": true,
      "content": {},
      "collaborators": {},
      "_expandable": {
        "content": "string",
        "collaborators": "string"
      },
      "_links": {
        "property1": {},
        "property2": {}
      },
      "contentTypeModified": true,
      "confRev": "string",
      "syncRev": "string",
      "syncRevSource": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment/{attachmentId}`

Updates the attachment properties, i.e. the non-binary data of an attachment
like the filename, media-type, comment, and parent container.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "container": {},
  "metadata": {
    "mediaType": "string"
  },
  "extensions": {},
  "version": {
    "by": {},
    "when": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "friendlyWhen": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "number": 0,
    "minorEdit": true,
    "content": {},
    "collaborators": {},
    "_expandable": {
      "content": "string",
      "collaborators": "string"
    },
    "_links": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "contentTypeModified": true,
    "confRev": "string",
    "syncRev": "string",
    "syncRevSource": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-attachment-properties-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that the attachment is attached to.|
|attachmentId|path|string|true|The ID of the attachment to update.|
|body|body|[AttachmentPropertiesUpdateBody](#schemaattachmentpropertiesupdatebody)|true|The details of the attachment to be updated.|
|» id|body|string|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|Set this to "attachment"|
|» status|body|string|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|none|
|» container|body|[Container](#schemacontainer)|false|Container for content. This can be either a space (containing a page or blogpost)<br>or a page/blog post (containing an attachment or comment)|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » mediaType|body|string|false|none|
|» extensions|body|object|false|none|
|» version|body|[Version](#schemaversion)|true|none|

<h3 id="update-attachment-properties-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the attachment is updated.|[Content](#schemacontent)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- The attachment id is invalid.<br>- The attachment version number is invalid.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- The calling user is not permitted to update or move the attachment.<br>- The attachment is being moved to an invalid content type.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if no attachment is found for the attachment ID.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the version of the supplied attachment does not match<br>the version of the attachment stored in the database.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-file write:confluence-props )
</aside>

## Update attachment data

<a id="opIdupdateAttachmentData"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/child/attachment/string/data \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'comment=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'minorEdit=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment/{attachmentId}/data`

Updates the binary data of an attachment, given the attachment ID, and
optionally the comment and the minor edit field.

This method is essentially the same as [Create or update attachments](#api-content-id-child-attachment-put),
except that it matches the attachment ID rather than the name.

Note, you must set a `X-Atlassian-Token: nocheck` header on the request
for this method, otherwise it will be blocked. This protects against XSRF
attacks, which is necessary as this method accepts multipart/form-data.

The media type 'multipart/form-data' is defined in [RFC 7578](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7578.txt).
Most client libraries have classes that make it easier to implement
multipart posts, like the [MultipartEntityBuilder](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-client-5.1.x/current/httpclient5/apidocs/)
Java class provided by Apache HTTP Components.

Note, according to [RFC 7578](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7578#section-4.5),
in the case where the form data is text,
the charset parameter for the "text/plain" Content-Type may be used to
indicate the character encoding used in that part. In the case of this
API endpoint, the `comment` body parameter should be sent with `type=text/plain`
and `charset=utf-8` values. This will force the charset to be UTF-8.

Example: This curl command updates an attachment (id='att456') that is attached
to a piece of content (id='123') with a comment and `minorEdits`=true.

``` bash
curl -D- \
  -u admin:admin \
  -X POST \
  -H 'X-Atlassian-Token: nocheck' \
  -F 'file=@"example.txt"' \
  -F 'minorEdit="true"' \
  -F 'comment="Example attachment comment"; type=text/plain; charset=utf-8' \
  http://myhost/rest/api/content/123/child/attachment/att456/data
```
**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
comment: string
minorEdit: string
```

<h3 id="update-attachment-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that the attachment is attached to.|
|attachmentId|path|string|true|The ID of the attachment to update.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The relative location and name of the attachment to be added to<br>the content.|
|» comment|body|string(binary)|false|The comment for the attachment that is being added.<br>If you specify a comment, then every file must have a comment and<br>the comments must be in the same order as the files. Alternatively,<br>don't specify any comments.|
|» minorEdit|body|string(binary)|true|If `minorEdits` is set to 'true', no notification email or activity stream<br>will be generated when the attachment is added to the content.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|404|Not Found|Returned if no attachment is found for the attachment ID.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-file )
</aside>

## Get URI to download attachment

<a id="opIddownloadAttatchment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/child/attachment/string/download \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment/{attachmentId}/download`

Redirects the client to a URL that serves an attachment's binary data.

<h3 id="get-uri-to-download-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that the attachment is attached to.|
|attachmentId|path|string|true|The ID of the attachment to download.|
|version|query|integer|false|The version of the attachment. If this parameter is absent, the redirect URI will download the latest version of the attachment.|
|status|query|[string]|false|The statuses allowed on the retrieved attachment. If this parameter is absent, it will default to `current`.|

<h3 id="get-uri-to-download-attachment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|302|Found|Returned if download URL is found.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if version number is greater than attachment's latest version number or an invalid value.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if there are authentication issues in request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- No content is found with the specified content ID.<br>- The specified content does not contain an attachment with the specified attachment ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the attachment.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: readonly:content.attachment:confluence )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content-body">Content body</h1>

## Asynchronously convert content body

<a id="opIdasyncConvertContentBodyRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/contentbody/convert/async/export_view \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "value": "string",
    "representation": "view"
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/contentbody/convert/async/{to}`

Converts a content body from one format to another format asynchronously.
Returns the asyncId for the asynchronous task.

Supported conversions:

- atlas_doc_format: editor, export_view, storage, styled_view, view
- storage: atlas_doc_format, editor, export_view, styled_view, view
- editor: storage

No other conversions are supported at the moment.
Once a conversion is completed, it will be available for 5 minutes at the result endpoint.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
If request specifies 'contentIdContext', 'View' permission for the space, and permission to view the content.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": "string",
  "representation": "view"
}
```

<h3 id="asynchronously-convert-content-body-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|to|path|string|true|The name of the target format for the content body.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand and populate. Expands are dependent on the<br>`to` conversion format and may be irrelevant for certain conversions (e.g. `macroRenderedOutput` is redundant when<br>converting to `view` format). <br><br>If rendering to `view` format, and the body content being converted includes arbitrary nested content (such as macros); then it is <br>necessary to include webresource expands in the request. Webresources for content body are the batched JS and CSS dependencies for<br>any nested dynamic content (i.e. macros).<br><br>- `embeddedContent` returns metadata for nested content (e.g. page included using page include macro)<br>- `mediaToken` returns JWT token for retrieving attachment data from Media API<br>- `macroRenderedOutput` additionally converts body to view format<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.js` returns all common JS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.all` returns all common dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.all` returns all common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.js` returns all common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.uris.js` returns JS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.css` returns CSS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.all` returns all dependencies specific to conversion     <br>- `webresource.tags.all` returns common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.css` returns common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.js` returns common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags|
|spaceKeyContext|query|string|false|The space key used for resolving embedded content (page includes,<br>files, and links) in the content body. For example, if the source content<br>contains the link `<ac:link><ri:page ri:content-title="Example page" /><ac:link>`<br>and the `spaceKeyContext=TEST` parameter is provided, then the link<br>will be converted to a link to the "Example page" page in the "TEST" space.|
|contentIdContext|query|string|false|The content ID used to find the space for resolving embedded content<br>(page includes, files, and links) in the content body. For example,<br>if the source content contains the link `<ac:link><ri:page ri:content-title="Example page" /><ac:link>`<br>and the `contentIdContext=123` parameter is provided, then the link<br>will be converted to a link to the "Example page" page in the same space<br>that has the content with ID=123. Note, `spaceKeyContext` will be ignored<br>if this parameter is provided.|
|allowCache|query|boolean|false|Controls whether conversion results are cached and reused for identical requests.<br><br>- `false`: Each request creates a new conversion task, even if an identical request was made previously.<br>- `true`: Enables caching behavior for identical requests from the same user.<br>  - If no cached result exists, a new conversion task is created<br>  - If a cached result exists, the existing task is marked as RERUNNING and will complete with status COMPLETED<br>  - Returns the same task ID for identical requests, allowing you to retrieve the cached result|
|embeddedContentRender|query|string|false|Mode used for rendering embedded content, like attachments.<br><br>- `current` renders the embedded content using the latest version.<br>- `version-at-save` renders the embedded content using the version at<br>the time of save.|
|body|body|[ContentBodyCreate](#schemacontentbodycreate)|true|The content body to convert.|
|» value|body|string|true|The body of the content in the relevant format.|
|» representation|body|string|true|The content format type. Set the value of this property to<br>the name of the format being used, e.g. 'storage'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|to|export_view|
|embeddedContentRender|current|
|embeddedContentRender|version-at-save|
|» representation|view|
|» representation|export_view|
|» representation|styled_view|
|» representation|storage|
|» representation|editor|
|» representation|editor2|
|» representation|anonymous_export_view|
|» representation|wiki|
|» representation|atlas_doc_format|
|» representation|plain|
|» representation|raw|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asyncId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="asynchronously-convert-content-body-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the content is added to the messaging queue for conversion. This id will be available for 5 minutes after the conversion is complete.|[AsyncId](#schemaasyncid)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned<br>- if the content body or conversion context is invalid or null<br>- if the value is improperly formed<br>- any conversion type other than export_view|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if content cannot be found with the provided context.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.all )
</aside>

## Get asynchronously converted content body from the id or the current status of the task.

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/contentbody/convert/async/{id}`

Returns the content body for the corresponding `asyncId` of a completed conversion task. If
the task is not completed, the task status is returned instead.

Once a conversion task is completed, the result can be obtained for up to 5 minutes, or

## Create asynchronous content body conversion tasks in bulk

<a id="opIdbulkAsyncConvertContentBodyRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/contentbody/convert/async/bulk/tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "conversionInputs": [
      {
        "to": "string",
        "allowCache": false,
        "spaceKeyContext": "string",
        "contentIdContext": "string",
        "embeddedContentRender": "current",
        "expand": [
          "string"
        ],
        "body": {
          "value": "string",
          "representation": "view"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/contentbody/convert/async/bulk/tasks`

Asynchronously converts content bodies from one format to another format in bulk. Use the Content body
REST API to get the status of conversion tasks. Note that there is a maximum limit of 10 conversions per
request to this endpoint.

Supported conversions:

- storage: editor, export_view, styled_view, view
- editor: storage

Once a conversion task is completed, it is available for polling for up to 5 minutes.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space, and permission to view the content if the `spaceKeyContext` or
`contentIdContext` are present.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversionInputs": [
    {
      "to": "string",
      "allowCache": false,
      "spaceKeyContext": "string",
      "contentIdContext": "string",
      "embeddedContentRender": "current",
      "expand": [
        "string"
      ],
      "body": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

|» conversionInputs|body|[[ContentBodyConversionInput](#schemacontentbodyconversioninput)]|false|none|

```json
  {
```
