<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content---children-and-descendants">Content - children and descendants</h1>

## Move a page to a new location relative to a target page

<a id="opIdmovePage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/move/before/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/content/{pageId}/move/{position}/{targetId}`

Move a page to a new location relative to a target page:

* `before` - move the page under the same parent as the target, before the target in the list of children
* `after` - move the page under the same parent as the target, after the target in the list of children
* `append` - move the page to be a child of the target

Caution: This API can move pages to the top level of a space. Top-level pages are difficult to find in the UI
because they do not show up in the page tree display. To avoid this, never use `before` or `after` positions
when the `targetId` is a top-level page.

<h3 id="move-a-page-to-a-new-location-relative-to-a-target-page-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageId|path|string|true|The ID of the page to be moved|
|position|path|string|true|The position to move the page to relative to the target page:<br>* `before` - move the page under the same parent as the target, before the target in the list of children<br>* `after` - move the page under the same parent as the target, after the target in the list of children<br>* `append` - move the page to be a child of the target|
|targetId|path|string|true|The ID of the target page for this operation|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|position|before|
|position|after|
|position|append|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "pageId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="move-a-page-to-a-new-location-relative-to-a-target-page-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Page was successfully moved|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- A page already exists in the target space with the same name.<br>  User is advised to rename page before moving.<br>- The move would create a parent-child loop (page becomes a descendant and ancestor of itself)<br>- The page has permission restrictions that the user does not have permission to create in the target space.<br>  User is advised to remove restrictions before moving.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- User does not have permission to remove page from current space<br>- User does not have permission to create a page in target space|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- The id or targetId refer to non-existent pages|None|

<h3 id="move-a-page-to-a-new-location-relative-to-a-target-page-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageId|[ContentId](#schemacontentid)|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Get content descendants

<a id="opIdgetContentDescendants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/descendant \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/descendant`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns a map of the descendants of a piece of content. This is similar
to [Get content children](#api-content-id-child-get), except that this
method returns child pages at all levels, rather than just the direct
child pages.

A piece of content has different types of descendants, depending on its type:

- `page`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `whiteboard`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `database`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `embed`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `folder`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `blogpost`: descendant is `comment`, `attachment`
- `attachment`: descendant is `comment`
- `comment`: descendant is `attachment`

The map will always include all descendant types that are valid for the content.
However, if the content has no instances of a descendant type, the map will
contain an empty array for that descendant type.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space, and permission to view the content if it
is a page.

<h3 id="get-content-descendants-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content to be queried for its descendants.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the children to<br>expand, where:<br><br>- `attachment` returns all attachments for the content.<br>- `comments` returns all comments for the content.<br>- `page` returns all child pages of the content.<br>- `whiteboard` returns all child whiteboards of the content.<br>- `database` returns all child databases of the content.<br>- `embed` returns all child embeds of the content.<br>- `folder` returns all child folders of the content.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|attachment|
|expand|comment|
|expand|page|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "attachment": {},
  "comment": {},
  "page": {},
  "whiteboard": {},
  "database": {},
  "embed": {},
  "folder": {},
  "_expandable": {
    "attachment": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "page": "string",
    "whiteboard": "string",
    "database": "string",
    "embed": "string",
    "folder": "string"
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-content-descendants-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested descendants are returned.|[ContentChildren](#schemacontentchildren)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Get content descendants by type

<a id="opIdgetDescendantsOfType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/descendant/page \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/descendant/{type}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns all descendants of a given type, for a piece of content. This is
similar to [Get content children by type](#api-content-id-child-type-get),
except that this method returns child pages at all levels, rather than just
the direct child pages.

A piece of content has different types of descendants, depending on its type:

- `page`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `whiteboard`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `database`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `embed`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `folder`: descendant is `page`, `whiteboard`, `database`, `embed`, `folder`, `comment`, `attachment`
- `blogpost`: descendant is `comment`, `attachment`
- `attachment`: descendant is `comment`
- `comment`: descendant is `attachment`

Custom content types that are provided by apps can also be returned.

If the expand query parameter is used with the `body.export_view` and/or `body.styled_view` properties, then the query limit parameter will be restricted to a maximum value of 25.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space, and permission to view the content if it
is a page.

<h3 id="get-content-descendants-by-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content to be queried for its descendants.|
|type|path|string|true|The type of descendants to return.|
|depth|query|string|false|Filter the results to descendants upto a desired level of the content. Note, the maximum value supported is 100. root level of the content means immediate (level 1) descendants of the type requested. all represents returning all descendants of the type requested.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand.<br><br>- `childTypes.all` returns whether the content has attachments, comments, or child pages/whiteboards.<br>Use this if you only need to check whether the content has children of a particular type.<br>- `childTypes.attachment` returns whether the content has attachments.<br>- `childTypes.comment` returns whether the content has comments.<br>- `childTypes.page` returns whether the content has child pages.<br>- `childTypes.whiteboard` returns whether the content has child whiteboards.<br>- `childTypes.database` returns whether the content has child databases.<br>- `childTypes.embed` returns whether the content has child embeds (smartlinks).<br>- `childTypes.folder` returns whether the content has child folders.<br>- `container` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information<br>returned by [Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br>- `metadata.currentuser` returns information about the current user in relation to the content,<br>including when they last viewed it, modified it, contributed to it, or added it as a favorite.<br>- `metadata.properties` returns content properties that have been set via the Confluence REST API.<br>- `metadata.labels` returns the labels that have been added to the content.<br>- `metadata.frontend` this property is only used by Atlassian.<br>- `operations` returns the operations for the content, which are used when setting permissions.<br>- `children.page` returns pages that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.database` returns databases that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.folder` returns folders that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.attachment` returns all attachments for the content.<br>- `children.comment` returns all comments on the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to read the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to read the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups, because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to update the content.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to update the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `history` returns the history of the content, including the date it was created.<br>- `history.lastUpdated` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including<br>who updated it and when it was updated.<br>- `history.previousVersion` returns information about the update prior to the current content update.<br>- `history.contributors` returns all of the users who have contributed to the content.<br>- `history.nextVersion` returns information about the update after to the current content update.<br>- `ancestors` returns the parent content, if the content is a page or whiteboard.<br>- `body` returns the body of the content in different formats, including the editor format,<br>view format, and export format.<br>- `body.storage` returns the body of content in storage format.<br>- `body.view` returns the body of content in view format.<br>- `version` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including who updated it<br>and when it was updated.<br>- `descendants.page` returns pages that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.database` returns databases that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.folder` returns folders that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.attachment` returns all attachments for the content, same as `children.attachment`.<br>- `descendants.comment` returns all comments on the content, same as `children.comment`.<br>- `space` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information returned by<br>[Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br><br>In addition, the following comment-specific expansions can be used:<br>- `extensions.inlineProperties` returns inline comment-specific properties.<br>- `extensions.resolution` returns the resolution status of each comment.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned content.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of content to return per page. Note,<br>this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|page|
|type|comment|
|type|attachment|
|depth|all|
|depth|root|
|depth|<any positive integer argument in the range of 1 and 100>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {}
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-content-descendants-by-type-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested content is returned.|[ContentArray](#schemacontentarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- Any of the required request params are missing.<br>- The request is invalid such as negative start param, a format besides int32 for limit etc.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Copy page hierarchy

<a id="opIdcopyPageHierarchy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/pagehierarchy/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "copyAttachments": false,
    "copyPermissions": false,
    "copyProperties": false,
    "copyLabels": false,
    "copyCustomContents": false,
    "copyDescendants": true,
    "destinationPageId": "string",
    "titleOptions": {
      "prefix": "string",
      "replace": "string",
      "search": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/pagehierarchy/copy`

Copy page hierarchy allows the copying of an entire hierarchy of pages and their associated properties, permissions and attachments.
 The id path parameter refers to the content id of the page to copy, and the new parent of this copied page is defined using the destinationPageId in the request body.
 The titleOptions object defines the rules of renaming page titles during the copy;
 for example, search and replace can be used in conjunction to rewrite the copied page titles.

 Response example:
 <pre><code>
 {
      "id" : "1180606",
      "links" : {
           "status" : "/rest/api/longtask/1180606"
      }
 }
 </code></pre>
 Use the /longtask/<taskId> REST API to get the copy task status.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "copyAttachments": false,
  "copyPermissions": false,
  "copyProperties": false,
  "copyLabels": false,
  "copyCustomContents": false,
  "copyDescendants": true,
  "destinationPageId": "string",
  "titleOptions": {
    "prefix": "string",
    "replace": "string",
    "search": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="copy-page-hierarchy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[CopyPageHierarchyRequest](#schemacopypagehierarchyrequest)|true|Request object from json post body|
|» copyAttachments|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, attachments are copied to the destination page.|
|» copyPermissions|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, page permissions are copied to the destination page.|
|» copyProperties|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, content properties are copied to the destination page.|
|» copyLabels|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, labels are copied to the destination page.|
|» copyCustomContents|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, custom contents are copied to the destination page.|
|» copyDescendants|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, descendants are copied to the destination page.|
|» destinationPageId|body|[ContentId](#schemacontentid)|true|none|
|» titleOptions|body|[CopyPageHierarchyTitleOptions](#schemacopypagehierarchytitleoptions)|false|Required for copying page in the same space.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "ari": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "links": {
    "status": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="copy-page-hierarchy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Returns a full JSON representation of a long running task|[LongTask](#schemalongtask)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the title prefix is invalid (e.g. is empty, creates a conflict)|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to create content at source and destination|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if original page or destination page does not exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Copy single page

<a id="opIdcopyPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "copyAttachments": false,
    "copyPermissions": false,
    "copyProperties": false,
    "copyLabels": false,
    "copyCustomContents": false,
    "destination": {
      "type": "space",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "pageTitle": "string",
    "body": {
      "storage": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "editor2": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/copy`

Copies a single page and its associated properties, permissions, attachments, and custom contents.
 The `id` path parameter refers to the content ID of the page to copy. The target of the page to be copied
 is defined using the `destination` in the request body and can be one of the following types.

  - `space`: page will be copied to the specified space as a root page on the space
  - `parent_page`: page will be copied as a child of the specified parent page
  - `parent_content`: page will be copied as a child of the specified parent content
  - `existing_page`: page will be copied and replace the specified page

By default, the following objects are expanded: `space`, `history`, `version`.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**: 'Add' permission for the space that the content will be copied in and permission to update the content if copying to an `existing_page`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "copyAttachments": false,
  "copyPermissions": false,
  "copyProperties": false,
  "copyLabels": false,
  "copyCustomContents": false,
  "destination": {
    "type": "space",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "pageTitle": "string",
  "body": {
    "storage": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "editor2": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    }
  }
}
```

This is the same as the information<br>returned by [Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br>- `metadata.currentuser` returns information about the current user in relation to the content,<br>including when they last viewed it, modified it, contributed to it, or added it as a favorite.<br>- `metadata.properties` returns content properties that have been set via the Confluence REST API.<br>- `metadata.labels` returns the labels that have been added to the content.<br>- `metadata.frontend` this property is only used by Atlassian.<br>- `operations` returns the operations for the content, which are used when setting permissions.<br>- `children.page` returns pages that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.database` returns databases that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.folder` returns folders that are descendants at the level immediately below the content.<br>- `children.attachment` returns all attachments for the content.<br>- `children.comment` returns all comments on the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to read the content.<br>- `restrictions.read.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to read the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups, because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.user` returns the users that have permission to update the content.<br>- `restrictions.update.restrictions.group` returns the groups that have permission to update the content. Note that<br>this may return deleted groups because deleting a group doesn't remove associated restrictions.<br>- `history` returns the history of the content, including the date it was created.<br>- `history.lastUpdated` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including<br>who updated it and when it was updated.<br>- `history.previousVersion` returns information about the update prior to the current content update.<br>- `history.contributors` returns all of the users who have contributed to the content.<br>- `history.nextVersion` returns information about the update after to the current content update.<br>- `ancestors` returns the parent content, if the content is a page or whiteboard.<br>- `body` returns the body of the content in different formats, including the editor format,<br>view format, and export format.<br>- `body.storage` returns the body of content in storage format.<br>- `body.view` returns the body of content in view format.<br>- `version` returns information about the most recent update of the content, including who updated it<br>and when it was updated.<br>- `descendants.page` returns pages that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.whiteboard` returns whiteboards that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.database` returns databases that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.embed` returns embeds (smartlinks) that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.folder` returns folders that are descendants at any level below the content.<br>- `descendants.attachment` returns all attachments for the content, same as `children.attachment`.<br>- `descendants.comment` returns all comments on the content, same as `children.comment`.<br>- `space` returns the space that the content is in. This is the same as the information returned by<br>[Get space](#api-space-spaceKey-get).<br><br>In addition, the following comment-specific expansions can be used:<br>- `extensions.inlineProperties` returns inline comment-specific properties.<br>- `extensions.resolution` returns the resolution status of each comment.|
|body|body|[CopyPageRequest](#schemacopypagerequest)|true|Request object from json post body|

|» body|body|object|false|If defined, this will replace the body of the destination page.|
|» » storage|body|[ContentBodyCreate](#schemacontentbodycreate)|false|This object is used when creating or updating content.|
|» » editor2|body|[ContentBodyCreate](#schemacontentbodycreate)|false|This object is used when creating or updating content.|

<h3 id="copy-single-page-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the content is copied.|[Content](#schemacontent)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- destination or any of its fields are not specified.<br>- destination.type is invalid.<br>- sub-expansions limit exceeds.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to create content at destination.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- the original page doesn't exist.<br>- the destination page doesn’t exist.<br>- the destination space doesn’t exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content---macro-body">Content - macro body</h1>

## Get macro body by macro ID

<a id="opIdgetMacroBodyByMacroId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/history/0/macro/id/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/history/{version}/macro/id/{macroId}`

Returns the body of a macro in storage format, for the given macro ID.
This includes information like the name of the macro, the body of the macro,
and any macro parameters. This method is mainly used by Cloud apps.

About the macro ID: When a macro is created in a new version of content,
Confluence will generate a random ID for it, unless an ID is specified
(by an app). The macro ID will look similar to this: '50884bd9-0cb8-41d5-98be-f80943c14f96'.
The ID is then persisted as new versions of content are created, and is
only modified by Confluence if there are conflicting IDs.

For Forge macros, the value for macro ID is the "local ID" of that particular ADF node.
This value can be retrieved either client-side by calling view.getContext() and accessing "localId"
on the resulting object, or server-side by examining the "local-id" parameter node inside the "parameters" node.

Note that there are other attributes named "local-id", but only this particular one is used to store the macro ID.

Example:
<ac:adf-node type="extension">
  <ac:adf-attribute key="extension-type">com.atlassian.ecosystem</ac:adf-attribute>
  <ac:adf-attribute key="parameters">
      <ac:adf-parameter key="local-id">e9c4aa10-73fa-417c-888d-48c719ae4165</ac:adf-parameter>
  </ac:adf-parameter>
</ac:adf-node>

Note, to preserve backwards compatibility this resource will also match on
the hash of the macro body, even if a macro ID is found. This check will
eventually become redundant, as macro IDs are generated for pages and
transparently propagate out to all instances.

This backwards compatibility logic does not apply to Forge macros; those
can only be retrieved by their ID.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the content that the macro is in.

<h3 id="get-macro-body-by-macro-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID for the content that contains the macro.|
|version|path|integer(int32)|true|The version of the content that contains the macro. Specifying `0` as the `version` will return<br>the macro body for the latest content version.|
|macroId|path|string|true|The ID of the macro. This is usually passed by the app that the<br>macro is in. Otherwise, find the macro ID by querying the desired<br>content and version, then expanding the body in storage format.<br>For example, '/content/196611/version/7?expand=content.body.storage'.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "body": "string",
  "parameters": {},
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-macro-body-by-macro-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested macro body is returned.|[MacroInstance](#schemamacroinstance)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the content.<br>- The macro does not exist in the specified version.<br>- There is no macro matching the given macro ID or hash.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.all )
</aside>

## Get macro body by macro ID and convert the representation synchronously

<a id="opIdgetAndConvertMacroBodyByMacroId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/history/0/macro/id/string/convert/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/history/{version}/macro/id/{macroId}/convert/{to}`

Returns the body of a macro in format specified in path, for the given macro ID.
This includes information like the name of the macro, the body of the macro,
and any macro parameters.

About the macro ID: When a macro is created in a new version of content,
Confluence will generate a random ID for it, unless an ID is specified
(by an app). The macro ID will look similar to this: '50884bd9-0cb8-41d5-98be-f80943c14f96'.
The ID is then persisted as new versions of content are created, and is
only modified by Confluence if there are conflicting IDs.

For Forge macros, the value for macro ID is the "local ID" of that particular ADF node.
This value can be retrieved either client-side by calling view.getContext() and accessing "localId"
on the resulting object, or server-side by examining the "local-id" parameter node inside the "parameters" node.

Note that there are other attributes named "local-id", but only this particular one is used to store the macro ID.

Example:
<ac:adf-node type="extension">
  <ac:adf-attribute key="extension-type">com.atlassian.ecosystem</ac:adf-attribute>
  <ac:adf-attribute key="parameters">
      <ac:adf-parameter key="local-id">e9c4aa10-73fa-417c-888d-48c719ae4165</ac:adf-parameter>
  </ac:adf-parameter>
</ac:adf-node>

Note, to preserve backwards compatibility this resource will also match on
the hash of the macro body, even if a macro ID is found. This check will
eventually become redundant, as macro IDs are generated for pages and
transparently propagate out to all instances.

This backwards compatibility logic does not apply to Forge macros; those
can only be retrieved by their ID.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the content that the macro is in.

<h3 id="get-macro-body-by-macro-id-and-convert-the-representation-synchronously-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID for the content that contains the macro.|
|version|path|integer(int32)|true|The version of the content that contains the macro. Specifying `0` as the `version` will return<br>the macro body for the latest content version.|
|macroId|path|string|true|The ID of the macro. This is usually passed by the app that the<br>macro is in. Otherwise, find the macro ID by querying the desired<br>content and version, then expanding the body in storage format.<br>For example, '/content/196611/version/7?expand=content.body.storage'.|
|to|path|string|true|The content representation to return the macro in.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand and populate. Expands are dependent on the<br>`to` conversion format and may be irrelevant for certain conversions (e.g. `macroRenderedOutput` is redundant when<br>converting to `view` format). <br><br>If rendering to `view` format, and the body content being converted includes arbitrary nested content (such as macros); then it is <br>necessary to include webresource expands in the request. Webresources for content body are the batched JS and CSS dependencies for<br>any nested dynamic content (i.e. macros).<br><br>- `embeddedContent` returns metadata for nested content (e.g. page included using page include macro)<br>- `mediaToken` returns JWT token for retrieving attachment data from Media API<br>- `macroRenderedOutput` additionally converts body to view format<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.js` returns all common JS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.all` returns all common dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.all` returns all common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.js` returns all common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.uris.js` returns JS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.css` returns CSS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.all` returns all dependencies specific to conversion     <br>- `webresource.tags.all` returns common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.css` returns common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.js` returns common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags|
|spaceKeyContext|query|string|false|The space key used for resolving embedded content (page includes,<br>files, and links) in the content body. For example, if the source content<br>contains the link `<ac:link><ri:page ri:content-title="Example page" /><ac:link>`<br>and the `spaceKeyContext=TEST` parameter is provided, then the link<br>will be converted to a link to the "Example page" page in the "TEST" space.|
|embeddedContentRender|query|string|false|Mode used for rendering embedded content, like attachments.<br><br>- `current` renders the embedded content using the latest version.<br>- `version-at-save` renders the embedded content using the version at<br>the time of save.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|embeddedContentRender|current|
|embeddedContentRender|version-at-save|

## Get macro body by macro ID and convert representation Asynchronously

<a id="opIdgetAndAsyncConvertMacroBodyByMacroId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/history/0/macro/id/string/convert/async/export_view \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/history/{version}/macro/id/{macroId}/convert/async/{to}`

Returns Async Id of the conversion task which will convert the macro into a content body of the desired format.
The result will be available for 5 minutes after completion of the conversion.

About the macro ID: When a macro is created in a new version of content,
Confluence will generate a random ID for it, unless an ID is specified
(by an app). The macro ID will look similar to this: '884bd9-0cb8-41d5-98be-f80943c14f96'.
The ID is then persisted as new versions of content are created, and is
only modified by Confluence if there are conflicting IDs.

For Forge macros, the value for macro ID is the "local ID" of that particular ADF node.
This value can be retrieved either client-side by calling view.getContext() and accessing "localId"
on the resulting object, or server-side by examining the "local-id" parameter node inside the "parameters" node.

Note that there are other attributes named "local-id", but only this particular one is used to store the macro ID.

Example:
<ac:adf-node type="extension">
  <ac:adf-attribute key="extension-type">com.atlassian.ecosystem</ac:adf-attribute>
  <ac:adf-attribute key="parameters">
      <ac:adf-parameter key="local-id">e9c4aa10-73fa-417c-888d-48c719ae4165</ac:adf-parameter>
  </ac:adf-parameter>
</ac:adf-node>

Note, to preserve backwards compatibility this resource will also match on
the hash of the macro body, even if a macro ID is found. This check will
eventually become redundant, as macro IDs are generated for pages and
transparently propagate out to all instances.

This backwards compatibility logic does not apply to Forge macros; those
can only be retrieved by their ID.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the content that the macro is in.

<h3 id="get-macro-body-by-macro-id-and-convert-representation-asynchronously-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID for the content that contains the macro.|
|version|path|integer(int32)|true|The version of the content that contains the macro. Specifying `0` as the `version` will return<br>the macro body for the latest content version.|
|macroId|path|string|true|The ID of the macro. For apps, this is passed to the macro by the Connect/Forge framework.<br>Otherwise, find the macro ID by querying the desired<br>content and version, then expanding the body in storage format.<br>For example, '/content/196611/version/7?expand=content.body.storage'.|
|to|path|string|true|The content representation to return the macro in.<br>Currently, the following conversions are allowed:<br><br>- `export_view`<br>- `styled_view`<br>- `view`|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand and populate. Expands are dependent on the<br>`to` conversion format and may be irrelevant for certain conversions (e.g. `macroRenderedOutput` is redundant when<br>converting to `view` format). <br><br>If rendering to `view` format, and the body content being converted includes arbitrary nested content (such as macros); then it is <br>necessary to include webresource expands in the request. Webresources for content body are the batched JS and CSS dependencies for<br>any nested dynamic content (i.e. macros).<br><br>- `embeddedContent` returns metadata for nested content (e.g. page included using page include macro)<br>- `mediaToken` returns JWT token for retrieving attachment data from Media API<br>- `macroRenderedOutput` additionally converts body to view format<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.js` returns all common JS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.all` returns all common dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.all` returns all common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.js` returns all common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.uris.js` returns JS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.css` returns CSS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.all` returns all dependencies specific to conversion     <br>- `webresource.tags.all` returns common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.css` returns common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.js` returns common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags|
|allowCache|query|boolean|false|Controls whether conversion results are cached and reused for identical requests.<br><br>- `false`: Each request creates a new conversion task, even if an identical request was made previously.<br>- `true`: Enables caching behavior for identical requests from the same user.<br>  - If no cached result exists, a new conversion task is created<br>  - If a cached result exists, the existing task is marked as RERUNNING and will complete with status COMPLETED<br>  - Returns the same task ID for identical requests, allowing you to retrieve the cached result<br><br>For large macros that are slow to convert and for which it is acceptable to show cached data, set this field to `true`.|
|spaceKeyContext|query|string|false|The space key used for resolving embedded content (page includes,<br>files, and links) in the content body. For example, if the source content<br>contains the link `<ac:link><ri:page ri:content-title="Example page" /><ac:link>`<br>and the `spaceKeyContext=TEST` parameter is provided, then the link<br>will be converted to a link to the "Example page" page in the "TEST" space.|
|embeddedContentRender|query|string|false|Mode used for rendering embedded content, like attachments.<br><br>- `current` renders the embedded content using the latest version.<br>- `version-at-save` renders the embedded content using the version at<br>the time of save.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|to|export_view|
|to|view|
|to|styled_view|
|embeddedContentRender|current|
|embeddedContentRender|version-at-save|

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content-labels">Content labels</h1>

## Add labels to content

<a id="opIdaddLabelsToContent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/label \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "prefix": "string",
      "name": "string"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/label`

Adds labels to a piece of content. Does not modify the existing labels.

Notes:

- Labels can also be added when creating content ([Create content](#api-content-post)).
- Labels can be updated when updating content ([Update content](#api-content-id-put)).
This will delete the existing labels and replace them with the labels in
the request.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "prefix": "string",
    "name": "string"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="add-labels-to-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that will have labels added to it.|
|body|body|[LabelCreateArray](#schemalabelcreatearray) \| [LabelCreate](#schemalabelcreate)|true|The labels to add to the content.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[LabelCreateArray](#schemalabelcreatearray)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[LabelCreate](#schemalabelcreate)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "prefix": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "label": "string"
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-labels-to-content-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the labels are added to the content.|[LabelArray](#schemalabelarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- The body contains labels with invalid characters or too many characters.<br>- The body contains too many labels.<br>- The target content would contain too many labels after the operation.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to edit labels.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user can view but not edit the content.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Remove label from content using query parameter

<a id="opIdremoveLabelFromContentUsingQueryParameter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/label?name=string' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/label`

Removes a label from a piece of content. Labels can't be deleted from archived content.
This is similar to [Remove label from content](#api-content-id-label-label-delete)
except that the label name is specified via a query parameter.

Use this method if the label name has "/" characters, as
[Remove label from content using query parameter](#api-content-id-label-delete)
does not accept "/" characters for the label name.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

<h3 id="remove-label-from-content-using-query-parameter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that the label will be removed from.|
|name|query|string|true|The name of the label to be removed.|

<h3 id="remove-label-from-content-using-query-parameter-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the label is removed. The response body will be empty.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user can view but not edit the content.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Remove label from content

<a id="opIdremoveLabelFromContent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/label/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/label/{label}`

Removes a label from a piece of content. Labels can't be deleted from archived content.
This is similar to [Remove label from content using query parameter](#api-content-id-label-delete)
except that the label name is specified via a path parameter.

Use this method if the label name does not have "/" characters, as the path
parameter does not accept "/" characters for security reasons. Otherwise,
use [Remove label from content using query parameter](#api-content-id-label-delete).

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

<h3 id="remove-label-from-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that the label will be removed from.|
|label|path|string|true|The name of the label to be removed.|

<h3 id="remove-label-from-content-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the label is removed. The response body will be empty.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the label name has a "/" character.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user can view but not edit the content.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content-permissions">Content permissions</h1>

## Check content permissions

<a id="opIdcheckContentPermission"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/permission/check \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "subject": {
      "type": "user",
      "identifier": "string"
    },
    "operation": "read"
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/permission/check`

Check if a user or a group can perform an operation to the specified content. The `operation` to check
must be provided. The user’s account ID or the ID of the group can be provided in the `subject` to check
permissions against a specified user or group. The following permission checks are done to make sure that the
user or group has the proper access:

- site permissions
- space permissions
- content restrictions

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission) if checking permission for self,
otherwise 'Confluence Administrator' global permission is required.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subject": {
    "type": "user",
    "identifier": "string"
  },
  "operation": "read"
}
```

<h3 id="check-content-permissions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content to check permissions against.|
|body|body|[ContentPermissionRequest](#schemacontentpermissionrequest)|true|The content permission request.|
|» subject|body|[PermissionSubjectWithGroupId](#schemapermissionsubjectwithgroupid)|true|The user or group that the permission applies to.|
|» operation|body|string|true|The content permission operation to check.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» operation|read|
|» operation|update|
|» operation|delete|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "hasPermission": true,
  "errors": [
    {

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/restriction`

## Update restrictions

<a id="opIdupdateRestrictions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/restriction \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "results": [
      {
        "operation": "update",
        "restrictions": {
          "user": {
            "results": [
              {
                "accountId": "<account-id-1>"
              },
              {
                "accountId": "<account-id-2>"
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "operation": "read",
        "restrictions": {
          "user": {
            "results": [
              {
                "accountId": "<account-id-1>"
              },
              {
                "accountId": "<account-id-2>"
              },
              {
                "accountId": "<viewer-account-id>"
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/restriction`

Updates restrictions for a piece of content. For each operation in the request,
the supplied `user` and `group` lists replace the corresponding existing lists.
Omitted operations and omitted user or group lists are preserved. An explicitly
empty list (`{"results": []}` or `[]`) clears that list.

Use `read` for viewing restrictions and `update` for editing restrictions.
While content remains view restricted, an editor must also be able to view it.
Removing an editor's `read` restriction while retaining their `update` restriction
returns `400`. Remove their `update` restriction too, or clear all `read`
restrictions to remove direct viewing restrictions. Restrictions inherited
from ancestors still apply.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to edit the content.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "operation": "update",
      "restrictions": {
        "user": {
          "results": [
            {
              "accountId": "<account-id-1>"
            },
            {
              "accountId": "<account-id-2>"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "operation": "read",
      "restrictions": {
        "user": {
          "results": [
            {
              "accountId": "<account-id-1>"
            },
            {
              "accountId": "<account-id-2>"
            },
            {
              "accountId": "<viewer-account-id>"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-restrictions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content to update restrictions for.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content<br>restrictions (returned in response) to expand.<br><br>- `restrictions.user` returns the users that the restrictions apply to.<br>Expanded by default.<br>- `restrictions.group` returns the groups that the restrictions apply to.<br>Expanded by default.<br>- `content` returns the piece of content that the restrictions are<br>applied to.|
|body|body|[ContentRestrictionAddOrUpdateArray](#schemacontentrestrictionaddorupdatearray)|true|Supply a `results` array containing one entry per operation (`read` or `update`).<br>Within `restrictions`, identify users by `accountId` and groups by `id`.<br>The top-level collection and each user or group collection may also be supplied<br>as a plain array instead of an object with a `results` array.<br><br>User profiles, personal spaces, pagination metadata, `_links`, and `_expandable`<br>are not required in the request. The `expand` parameter controls only the response.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» results|body|[[ContentRestrictionUpdate](#schemacontentrestrictionupdate)]|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[[ContentRestrictionUpdate](#schemacontentrestrictionupdate)]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|restrictions.user|
|expand|read.restrictions.user|
|expand|update.restrictions.user|
|expand|restrictions.group|
|expand|read.restrictions.group|
|expand|update.restrictions.group|
|expand|content|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "operation": "administer",
      "restrictions": {
        "user": {},
        "group": {
          "results": [
            {
              "type": "group",
              "name": "string",
              "id": "string",
              "usageType": "USERBASE_GROUP",
              "managedBy": "ADMINS",
              "_links": {
                "property1": {},
                "property2": {}
              }
            }
          ],
          "start": 0,
          "limit": 0,
          "size": 0
        },
        "_expandable": {
          "user": "string",
          "group": "string"
        }
      },
      "content": {},
      "_expandable": {
        "restrictions": "string",
        "content": "string"
      },
      "_links": {
        "property1": {},
        "property2": {}
      }
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "restrictionsHash": "string",
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-restrictions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested restrictions are updated.|[ContentRestrictionArray](#schemacontentrestrictionarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br><br>- The request is empty, repeats an operation, uses an unsupported operation,<br>  or specifies invalid users or groups.<br>- The resulting restrictions for a supplied operation are nonempty and do not<br>  include the calling user in the `user` list. Membership in a restricted group<br>  does not satisfy this check. Callers with super-admin permissions are exempt.<br>- An attempt is made to remove an editor's read restriction while retaining<br>  their update restriction and keeping the content view restricted.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to update restrictions<br>for the content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Add restrictions

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/restriction`

Adds the supplied users and groups to the content's restrictions, preserving
existing restrictions. Use `read` for viewing restrictions and `update` for
editing restrictions. Omitted or empty user and group lists add no restrictions.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:

}

The `expand` parameter controls only the response.|

## Get content restriction status for group

<a id="opIdgetIndividualGroupRestrictionStatusByGroupId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/restriction/byOperation/read/byGroupId/string \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/restriction/byOperation/{operationKey}/byGroupId/{groupId}`

Returns whether the specified content restriction applies to a group.
For example, if a page with `id=123` has a `read` restriction for the `123456` group id,
the following request will return `true`:

`/wiki/rest/api/content/123/restriction/byOperation/read/byGroupId/123456`

Note that a response of `true` does not guarantee that the group can view the page, as it does not account for
account-inherited restrictions, space permissions, or even product access. For more
information, see [Confluence permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw).

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the content.

<h3 id="get-content-restriction-status-for-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that the restriction applies to.|
|operationKey|path|string|true|The operation that the restriction applies to.|
|groupId|path|string|true|The id of the group to be queried for whether the content restriction<br>applies to it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|operationKey|read|
|operationKey|update|

<h3 id="get-content-restriction-status-for-group-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns true if the content restriction applies to the group. The response<br>will not return a response body.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to view the<br>content.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if<br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- An invalid operation or group is specified.<br>- Given groupId is blank or has invalid characters|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.all )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content-states">Content states</h1>

## Get content state

<a id="opIdgetContentState"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/state \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/state`

Gets the current content state of the draft or current version of content. To specify the draft version, set
the parameter status to draft, otherwise archived or current will get the relevant published state.
**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the content.

<h3 id="get-content-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of the content whose content state is of interest.|
|status|query|string|false|Set status to one of [current,draft,archived]. Default value is current.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|current|
|status|draft|
|status|archived|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "contentState": {
    "id": 0,
    "name": "string",
    "color": "string"
  },
  "lastUpdated": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-content-state-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if permission allows viewing of content.|[ContentStateResponse](#schemacontentstateresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if user does not have content view permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the content with given id can not be found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Set the content state of a content and publishes a new version of the content.

<a id="opIdsetContentState"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/state?status=current' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "color": "string",
    "id": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/state`

Sets the content state of the content specified and creates a new version
(publishes the content without changing the body) of the content with the new state.

You may pass in either an id of a state, or the name and color of a desired new state.
If all 3 are passed in, id will be used.
If the name and color passed in already exist under the current user's existing custom states, the existing state will be reused.
If custom states are disabled in the space of the content (which can be determined by getting the content state space settings of the content's space)
then this set will fail.

You may not remove a content state via this PUT request. You must use the DELETE method. A specified state is required in the body of this request.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to edit the content.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "color": "string",
  "id": 0
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-content-state-of-a-content-and-publishes-a-new-version-of-the-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The Id of the content whose content state is to be set.|
|status|query|string|true|Status of content onto which state will be placed. If draft, then draft state will change.<br>If current, state will be placed onto a new version of the content with same body as previous version.|
|body|body|[ContentStateRestInput](#schemacontentstaterestinput)|true|Content state fields for state. Pass in id for an existing state, or new name and color for best matching existing state, or new state if allowed in space.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of content state. Maximum 20 characters.|
|» color|body|string|false|Color of state. Must be in 6 digit hex form (#FFFFFF). The default colors offered in the UI are:<br> #ff7452 (red),<br> #2684ff (blue),<br> #ffc400 (yellow),<br> #57d9a3 (green), and<br> #8777d9 (purple)|
|» id|body|integer(int64)|false|id of state. This can be 0,1, or 2 if you wish to specify a default space state.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|current|
|status|draft|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "contentState": {
    "id": 0,
    "name": "string",
    "color": "string"
  },
  "lastUpdated": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-content-state-of-a-content-and-publishes-a-new-version-of-the-content-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if content state is set successfully.|[ContentStateResponse](#schemacontentstateresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid Name/Color, non-existent id of content state, or type of state desired is not allowed.<br>Name must be less than or exactly 20 characters. Color must be a valid hex string.<br>Status must be in [draft,current].|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if user does not have content edit permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the content with given id can not be found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[ContentState](#schemacontentstate)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-space.summary )
</aside>

## Get content state settings for space

<a id="opIdgetContentStateSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/state/settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/state/settings`

Get object describing whether content states are allowed at all, if custom content states or space content states
are restricted, and a list of space content states allowed for the space if they are not restricted.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

<h3 id="get-content-state-settings-for-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to be queried for its content state settings.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "contentStatesAllowed": true,
  "customContentStatesAllowed": true,
  "spaceContentStatesAllowed": true,
  "spaceContentStates": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "name": "string",
      "color": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-content-state-settings-for-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested space exists, and user has space admin permission.|[ContentStateSettings](#schemacontentstatesettings)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if user does not have space admin permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the space with given key can not be found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-space.summary )
</aside>

## Get content in space with given content state

<a id="opIdgetContentsWithState"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/state/content?state-id=0' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/state/content`

Returns all content that has the provided content state in a space.

If the expand query parameter is used with the `body.export_view` and/or `body.styled_view` properties, then the query limit parameter will be restricted to a maximum value of 25.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space.

<h3 id="get-content-in-space-with-given-content-state-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to be queried for its content state settings.|
|state-id|query|integer(int32)|true|The id of the content state to filter content by|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand.<br>Options include: space, version, history, children, etc.<br><br>Ex: space,version|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of results to return|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|Number of result to start returning. (0 indexed)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {}
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-content-in-space-with-given-content-state-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if search was successful.|[ContentArray](#schemacontentarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if limit or start are out of range, stateId is omitted.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if user does not have space view permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the space with given key can not be found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.all ), basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-content-versions">Content versions</h1>

## Restore content version

<a id="opIdrestoreContentVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/version \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "operationKey": "restore",
    "params": {
      "versionNumber": 0,
      "message": "string",
      "restoreTitle": false
    }
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/version`

Restores a historical version to be the latest version. That is, a new version
is created with the content of the historical version.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "operationKey": "restore",
  "params": {
    "versionNumber": 0,
    "message": "string",
    "restoreTitle": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="restore-content-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content for which the history will be restored.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand. By default, the `content`<br>object is expanded.<br><br>- `collaborators` returns the users that collaborated on the version.<br>- `content` returns the content for the version.|
|body|body|[VersionRestore](#schemaversionrestore)|true|The content version to be restored.|
|» operationKey|body|string|true|Set to 'restore'.|
|» params|body|object|true|none|
|» » versionNumber|body|integer(int32)|true|The version number to be restored.|
|» » message|body|string|true|Description for the version.|
|» » restoreTitle|body|boolean|false|If true, the content title will be the same as the title from the version restored. Defaults to `false`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» operationKey|restore|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "by": {},
  "when": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "friendlyWhen": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "number": 0,
  "minorEdit": true,
  "content": {},
  "collaborators": {},
  "_expandable": {
    "content": "string",
    "collaborators": "string"
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "contentTypeModified": true,
  "confRev": "string",
  "syncRev": "string",
  "syncRevSource": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="restore-content-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the version is restored.|[Version](#schemaversion)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- There is no version with the given version number.<br>- The version number is the current version.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user doesn't have permission to edit the<br>content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Delete content version

<a id="opIddeleteContentVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/version/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/version/{versionNumber}`

Delete a historical version. This does not delete the changes made to the
content in that version, rather the changes for the deleted version are
rolled up into the next version. Note, you cannot delete the current version.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

<h3 id="delete-content-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content that the version will be deleted from.|
|versionNumber|path|integer(int32)|true|The number of the version to be deleted. The version number starts<br>from 1 up to current version.|

<h3 id="delete-content-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the version is deleted.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- The content or version cannot be found.<br>- The current version is specified.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user doesn't have permission to edit the<br>content.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>
