## Get content watch status

<a id="opIdgetContentWatchStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/watch/content/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/user/watch/content/{contentId}`

Returns whether a user is watching a piece of content. Choose the user by
doing one of the following:

- Specify a user via a query parameter: Use the `accountId` to identify the user.
- Do not specify a user: The currently logged-in user will be used.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission or 'Space Administrator' permission for the relevant space if specifying a user, otherwise
permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="get-content-watch-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentId|path|string|true|The ID of the content to be queried for whether the specified user is<br>watching it.|
|key|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|username|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|accountId|query|string|false|The account ID of the user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products.<br>For example, `384093:32b4d9w0-f6a5-3535-11a3-9c8c88d10192`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "watching": true
}
```

<h3 id="get-content-watch-status-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested watch status is returned.|[UserWatch](#schemauserwatch)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the<br>content.<br>- A user is specified via a query parameter and the calling user is<br>not a Confluence administrator or space administrator.<br>- No content exists for the specified `contentId`.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if no `contentId` is specified.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Add content watcher

<a id="opIdaddContentWatcher"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/watch/content/string \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/user/watch/content/{contentId}`

Adds a user as a watcher to a piece of content. Choose the user by doing
one of the following:

- Specify a user via a query parameter: Use the `accountId` to identify the user.
- Do not specify a user: The currently logged-in user will be used.

Note, you must add the `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check` header when making a
request, as this operation has XSRF protection.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission or 'Space Administrator' permission for the relevant space if specifying a user, otherwise
permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="add-content-watcher-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentId|path|string|true|The ID of the content to add the watcher to.|
|key|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|username|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|accountId|query|string|false|The account ID of the user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products.<br>For example, `384093:32b4d9w0-f6a5-3535-11a3-9c8c88d10192`.|

<h3 id="add-content-watcher-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the watcher was successfully created. No response body is<br>returned.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- The `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check` header is not specified.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the<br>content.<br>- A user is specified via a query parameter and the calling user is<br>not a Confluence administrator or space administrator.<br>- No content exists for the specified `contentId`.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if no `contentId` is specified.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Remove content watcher

<a id="opIdremoveContentWatcher"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/watch/content/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -H 'X-Atlassian-Token: no-check'
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/user/watch/content/{contentId}`

Removes a user as a watcher from a piece of content. Choose the user by
doing one of the following:

- Specify a user via a query parameter: Use the `accountId` to identify the user.
- Do not specify a user: The currently logged-in user will be used.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Confluence Administrator' global permission or 'Space Administrator' permission for the relevant space if specifying a user, otherwise
permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="remove-content-watcher-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Atlassian-Token|header|string|true|Note, you must add header when making a<br>request, as this operation has XSRF protection.|
|contentId|path|string|true|The ID of the content to remove the watcher from.|
|key|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|username|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is no longer available and will be removed from the documentation soon.<br>Use `accountId` instead.<br>See the [deprecation notice](/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/) for details.|
|accountId|query|string|false|The account ID of the user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products.<br>For example, `384093:32b4d9w0-f6a5-3535-11a3-9c8c88d10192`.|

<h3 id="remove-content-watcher-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the watcher was successfully deleted. No response body is<br>returned.|None|

|404|Not Found|Returned if no `contentId` is specified.|None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Register modules

<a id="opIdregisterModules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/atlassian-connect/1/app/module/dynamic \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: */*' \
  -d '{"webItems":[{"key":"my-webitem","location":"system.admin/globalsettings","url":"/my-web-item","name":{"value":"My Web Item"}}],"adminPages":[{"key":"my-admin-page","name":{"value":"My Admin Page"},"url":"/my-admin-page"}]}'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/atlassian-connect/1/app/module/dynamic`

Registers a list of modules. For the list of modules that support dynamic registration, see [Dynamic modules](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/dynamic-modules/).

**[Permissions](#permissions) required:** Only Connect apps can make this request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "webItems": [
    {
      "key": "my-webitem",
      "location": "system.admin/globalsettings",
      "url": "/my-web-item",
      "name": {
        "value": "My Web Item"
      }
    }
  ],
  "adminPages": [
    {
      "key": "my-admin-page",
      "name": {
        "value": "My Admin Page"
      },
      "url": "/my-admin-page"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="register-modules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ConnectModules](#schemaconnectmodules)|true|none|
|» modules|body|[[ConnectModule](#schemaconnectmodule)]|true|A list of app modules in the same format as the `modules` property in the<br>[app descriptor](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/app-descriptor/).|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```text
Installation failed. The app com.example.app.key has duplicate module keys: [module-key]. Please contact the app vendor.
```

> 401 Response

```text
The request is not from a Connect app.
```

<h3 id="register-modules-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the request is successful.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if:<br>* any of the provided modules is invalid. For example, required properties are missing.<br>* any of the modules conflict with registered dynamic modules or modules defined in the app descriptor. For example, there are duplicate keys.<br><br>Details of the issues encountered are included in the error message.|[DynamicModulesErrorMessage](#schemadynamicmoduleserrormessage)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the call is not from a Connect app.|[DynamicModulesErrorMessage](#schemadynamicmoduleserrormessage)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-experimental">Experimental</h1>

APIs in this section can change without any prior deprecation notice.

## Delete page tree

<a id="opIddeletePageTree"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/content/string/pageTree \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/pageTree`

Moves a pagetree rooted at a page to the space's trash:

- If the content's type is `page` and its status is `current`, it will be trashed including
all its descendants.
- For every other combination of content type and status, this API is not supported.

This API accepts the pageTree delete request and returns a task ID.
The delete process happens asynchronously.

 Response example:
 <pre><code>
 {
      "id" : "1180606",
      "links" : {
           "status" : "/rest/api/longtask/1180606"
      }
 }
 </code></pre>
 Use the `/longtask/<taskId>` REST API to get the copy task status.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Delete' permission for the space that the content is in.

<h3 id="delete-page-tree-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the content which forms root of the page tree, to be deleted.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "ari": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "links": {
    "status": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-page-tree-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Returned if the request to trash content and all its current page descendants, is successfully accepted.|[LongTask](#schemalongtask)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the content id is invalid or id does not represents a 'CURRENT' page.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user can not delete the content with specified id.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no content with the given ID.<br>- The requesting user does not have permission to trash the content or any of it's descendant pages.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Get Space Labels

<a id="opIdgetLabelsForSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/label \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/label`

Returns a list of labels associated with a space. Can provide a prefix as well as other filters to
select different types of labels.

<h3 id="get-space-labels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to get labels for.|
|prefix|query|string|false|Filters the results to labels with the specified prefix. If this parameter<br>is not specified, then labels with any prefix will be returned.<br><br>- `global` prefix is used by labels that are on content within the provided space.<br>- `my` prefix can be explicitly added by a user when adding a label<br>via the UI, e.g. 'my:example-label'.<br>- `team` prefix is used for labels applied to the space.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned labels.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of labels to return per page. Note,<br>this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|prefix|global|
|prefix|my|
|prefix|team|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "prefix": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "label": "string"
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-space-labels-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the list of labels is returned.|[LabelArray](#schemalabelarray)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br>- There is no space with the given space key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-space.summary )
</aside>


`POST /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/label`

Adds labels to a piece of content. Does not modify the existing labels.

Notes:

- Labels can also be added when creating content ([Create content](#api-content-post)).
- Labels can be updated when updating content ([Update content](#api-content-id-put)).
This will delete the existing labels and replace them with the labels in
the request.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to update the content.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "prefix": "string",
    "name": "string"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="add-labels-to-a-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to add labels to.|
|body|body|[[LabelCreate](#schemalabelcreate)]|true|The labels to add to the content.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "prefix": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "label": "string"
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-labels-to-a-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the labels are added to the content.|[LabelArray](#schemalabelarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- The body contains labels with invalid characters or too many characters.<br>- The body contains too many labels.<br>- The target content would contain too many labels after the operation.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to edit labels.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user can view but not edit the content.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br>- There is no space with the given space key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-space )
</aside>

|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the calling user is not logged in to Confluence.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no task with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the task.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-space.summary )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-relation">Relation</h1>

## Find target entities related to a source entity

<a id="opIdfindTargetFromSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/relation/string/from/user/string/to/user \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/relation/{relationName}/from/{sourceType}/{sourceKey}/to/{targetType}`

Returns all target entities that have a particular relationship to the
source entity. Note, relationships are one way.

For example, the following method finds all content that the current user
has an 'ignore' relationship with:
`GET /wiki/rest/api/relation/ignore/from/user/current/to/content`
Note, 'ignore' is an example custom relationship type.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view both the target entity and source entity.

<h3 id="find-target-entities-related-to-a-source-entity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|relationName|path|string|true|The name of the relationship. This method supports relationships created via<br>[Create relationship](#api-wiki-rest-api-relation-relationname-from-sourcetype-sourcekey-to-targettype-targetkey-put).<br>Note, this method does not support 'like' or 'favourite' relationships.|
|sourceType|path|string|true|The source entity type of the relationship.|
|sourceKey|path|string|true|The identifier for the source entity:<br><br>- If `sourceType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|targetType|path|string|true|The target entity type of the relationship.|
|sourceStatus|query|string|false|The status of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content'.|
|targetStatus|query|string|false|The status of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content'.|
|sourceVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content' and the `sourceStatus` is 'historical'.|
|targetVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content' and the `targetStatus` is 'historical'.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the response<br>object to expand.<br><br>- `relationData` returns information about the relationship, such as<br>who created it and when it was created.<br>- `source` returns the source entity.<br>- `target` returns the target entity.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned relationships.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of relationships to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sourceType|user|
|sourceType|content|
|sourceType|space|
|targetType|user|
|targetType|content|
|targetType|space|
|expand|relationData|
|expand|source|
|expand|target|

<h3 id="find-target-entities-related-to-a-source-entity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested relationships are returned.|[RelationArray](#schemarelationarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to view the<br>relationships.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the target entity does not exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Find relationship from source to target

<a id="opIdgetRelationship"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/relation/string/from/user/string/to/user/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/relation/{relationName}/from/{sourceType}/{sourceKey}/to/{targetType}/{targetKey}`

Find whether a particular type of relationship exists from a source
entity to a target entity. Note, relationships are one way.

For example, you can use this method to find whether the current user has
selected a particular page as a favorite (i.e. 'save for later'):
`GET /wiki/rest/api/relation/favourite/from/user/current/to/content/123`

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view both the target entity and source entity.

<h3 id="find-relationship-from-source-to-target-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|relationName|path|string|true|The name of the relationship. This method supports the 'favourite'<br>(i.e. 'save for later') relationship as well as any other relationship<br>types created via [Create relationship](#api-wiki-rest-api-relation-relationname-from-sourcetype-sourcekey-to-targettype-targetkey-put).|
|sourceType|path|string|true|The source entity type of the relationship. This must be 'user', if<br>the `relationName` is 'favourite'.|
|sourceKey|path|string|true|- The identifier for the source entity:<br><br>- If `sourceType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|targetType|path|string|true|The target entity type of the relationship. This must be 'space' or<br>'content', if the `relationName` is 'favourite'.|
|targetKey|path|string|true|The identifier for the target entity:<br><br>- If `targetType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `targetType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `targetType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|sourceStatus|query|string|false|The status of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content'.|
|targetStatus|query|string|false|The status of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content'.|
|sourceVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content' and the `sourceStatus` is 'historical'.|
|targetVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content' and the `targetStatus` is 'historical'.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the response<br>object to expand.<br><br>- `relationData` returns information about the relationship, such as<br>who created it and when it was created.<br>- `source` returns the source entity.<br>- `target` returns the target entity.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sourceType|user|
|sourceType|content|
|sourceType|space|
|targetType|user|
|targetType|content|
|targetType|space|
|expand|relationData|
|expand|source|
|expand|target|

<h3 id="find-relationship-from-source-to-target-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the relationship exists.|[Relation](#schemarelation)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to view the<br>relationship.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the relationship does not exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Create relationship

<a id="opIdcreateRelationship"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/relation/string/from/user/string/to/user/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/relation/{relationName}/from/{sourceType}/{sourceKey}/to/{targetType}/{targetKey}`

Creates a relationship between two entities (user, space, content). The
'favourite' relationship is supported by default, but you can use this method
to create any type of relationship between two entities.

For example, the following method creates a 'sibling' relationship between
two pieces of content:
`PUT /wiki/rest/api/relation/sibling/from/content/123/to/content/456`

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="create-relationship-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|relationName|path|string|true|The name of the relationship. This method supports the 'favourite'<br>(i.e. 'save for later') relationship. You can also specify any other<br>value for this parameter to create a custom relationship type.|
|sourceType|path|string|true|The source entity type of the relationship. This must be 'user', if<br>the `relationName` is 'favourite'.|
|sourceKey|path|string|true|- The identifier for the source entity:<br><br>- If `sourceType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|targetType|path|string|true|The target entity type of the relationship. This must be 'space' or<br>'content', if the `relationName` is 'favourite'.|
|targetKey|path|string|true|- The identifier for the target entity:<br><br>- If `targetType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `targetType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `targetType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|sourceStatus|query|string|false|The status of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content'.|
|targetStatus|query|string|false|The status of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content'.|
|sourceVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content' and the `sourceStatus` is 'historical'.|
|targetVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content' and the `targetStatus` is 'historical'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sourceType|user|
|sourceType|content|
|sourceType|space|
|targetType|user|
|targetType|content|
|targetType|space|

<h3 id="create-relationship-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the relationship is created.|[Relation](#schemarelation)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to use Confluence.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the user, space or content could not be found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Delete relationship

<a id="opIddeleteRelationship"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/relation/string/from/user/string/to/user/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/relation/{relationName}/from/{sourceType}/{sourceKey}/to/{targetType}/{targetKey}`

Deletes a relationship between two entities (user, space, content).

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).
For favourite relationships, the current user can only delete their own
favourite relationships. A space administrator can delete favourite
relationships for any user.

<h3 id="delete-relationship-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|relationName|path|string|true|The name of the relationship.|
|sourceType|path|string|true|The source entity type of the relationship. This must be 'user', if<br>the `relationName` is 'favourite'.|
|sourceKey|path|string|true|- The identifier for the source entity:<br><br>- If `sourceType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `sourceType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|targetType|path|string|true|The target entity type of the relationship. This must be 'space' or<br>'content', if the `relationName` is 'favourite'.|
|targetKey|path|string|true|- The identifier for the target entity:<br><br>- If `targetType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `targetType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `targetType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|sourceStatus|query|string|false|The status of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content'.|
|targetStatus|query|string|false|The status of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content'.|
|sourceVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content' and the `sourceStatus` is 'historical'.|
|targetVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content' and the `targetStatus` is 'historical'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sourceType|user|
|sourceType|content|
|sourceType|space|
|targetType|user|
|targetType|content|
|targetType|space|

<h3 id="delete-relationship-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the relationship is deleted or the relationship didn't<br>exist.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to delete the<br>relationship.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the user, space or content could not be found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Find source entities related to a target entity

<a id="opIdfindSourcesForTarget"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/relation/string/to/user/string/from/user \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/relation/{relationName}/to/{targetType}/{targetKey}/from/{sourceType}`

Returns all target entities that have a particular relationship to the
source entity. Note, relationships are one way.

For example, the following method finds all users that have a 'collaborator'
relationship to a piece of content with an ID of '1234':
`GET /wiki/rest/api/relation/collaborator/to/content/1234/from/user`
Note, 'collaborator' is an example custom relationship type.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view both the target entity and source entity.

<h3 id="find-source-entities-related-to-a-target-entity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|relationName|path|string|true|The name of the relationship. This method supports relationships created via<br>[Create relationship](#api-wiki-rest-api-relation-relationname-from-sourcetype-sourcekey-to-targettype-targetkey-put).<br>Note, this method does not support 'like' or 'favourite' relationships.|
|sourceType|path|string|true|The source entity type of the relationship.|
|targetType|path|string|true|The target entity type of the relationship.|
|targetKey|path|string|true|The identifier for the target entity:<br><br>- If `targetType` is `user`, then specify either `current` (logged-in user), the user key of the user, or<br>the account ID of the user. Note that the user key has been deprecated in favor of the account ID for this parameter. See the<br>[migration guide](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-user-privacy-api-migration-guide/)<br>for details.<br>- If `targetType` is 'content', then specify the content ID.<br>- If `targetType` is 'space', then specify the space key.|
|sourceStatus|query|string|false|The status of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content'.|
|targetStatus|query|string|false|The status of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content'.|
|sourceVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the source. This parameter is only used when the<br>`sourceType` is 'content' and the `sourceStatus` is 'historical'.|
|targetVersion|query|integer(int32)|false|The version of the target. This parameter is only used when the<br>`targetType` is 'content' and the `targetStatus` is 'historical'.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the response<br>object to expand.<br><br>- `relationData` returns information about the relationship, such as<br>who created it and when it was created.<br>- `source` returns the source entity.<br>- `target` returns the target entity.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned relationships.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of relationships to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sourceType|user|
|sourceType|content|
|sourceType|space|
|targetType|user|
|targetType|content|
|targetType|space|
|expand|relationData|
|expand|source|
|expand|target|

<h3 id="find-source-entities-related-to-a-target-entity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested relationships are returned.|[RelationArray](#schemarelationarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request is invalid.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have permission to view the<br>relationship|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the target entity does not exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-search">Search</h1>

## Search content

<a id="opIdsearchByCQL"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/search?cql=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/search`

Searches for content using the
[Confluence Query Language (CQL)](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/advanced-searching-using-cql/).

**Note that CQL input queries submitted through the `/wiki/rest/api/search` endpoint no longer support user-specific fields like `user`, `user.fullname`, `user.accountid`, and `user.userkey`.** 
See this [deprecation notice](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/deprecation-notice-search-api/) for more details.

Example initial call:
```
/wiki/rest/api/search?cql=type=page&limit=25
```

Example response:
```
{
  "results": [
    { ... },
    { ... },
    ...
    { ... }
  ],
  "limit": 25,
  "size": 25,
  ...
  "_links": {
    "base": "<url>",
    "context": "<url>",
    "next": "/rest/api/search?cql=type=page&limit=25&cursor=raNDoMsTRiNg",
    "self": "<url>"
  }
}
```

When additional results are available, returns `next` and `prev` URLs to retrieve them in subsequent calls. The URLs each contain a cursor that points to the appropriate set of results. Use `limit` to specify the number of results returned in each call.

Example subsequent call (taken from example response):
```
/wiki/rest/api/search?cql=type=page&limit=25&cursor=raNDoMsTRiNg
```
The response to this will have a `prev` URL similar to the `next` in the example response.

If the expand query parameter is used with the `body.export_view` and/or `body.styled_view` properties, then the query limit parameter will be restricted to a maximum value of 25.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to view the entities. Note, only entities that the user has
permission to view will be returned.

<h3 id="search-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cql|query|string|true|The CQL query to be used for the search. See<br>[Advanced Searching using CQL](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/advanced-searching-using-cql/)<br>for instructions on how to build a CQL query.|
|cqlcontext|query|string|false|The space, content, and content status to execute the search<br>against.<br><br>- `spaceKey` Key of the space to search against. Optional.<br>- `contentId` ID of the content to search against. Optional. Must be<br>in the space specified by `spaceKey`.<br>- `contentStatuses` Content statuses to search against. Optional.<br><br>Specify these values in an object. For example,<br>`cqlcontext={%22spaceKey%22:%22TEST%22, %22contentId%22:%22123%22}`|
|cursor|query|string|false|Pointer to a set of search results, returned as part of the `next` or `prev` URL from the previous search call.|
|next|query|boolean|false|none|
|prev|query|boolean|false|none|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of content objects to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The start point of the collection to return|
|includeArchivedSpaces|query|boolean|false|Whether to include content from archived spaces in the results.|
|excludeCurrentSpaces|query|boolean|false|Whether to exclude current spaces and only show archived spaces.|
|excerpt|query|string|false|The excerpt strategy to apply to the result|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|query|string|false|Filters users by permission type. Use `none` to default to licensed users, `externalCollaborator`<br>for external/guest users, and `all` to include all permission types.|
|_|query|integer(int64)|false|none|
|expand|query|[string]|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|excerpt|highlight|
|excerpt|indexed|
|excerpt|none|
|excerpt|highlight_unescaped|
|excerpt|indexed_unescaped|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|all|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|externalCollaborator|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|none|

<h3 id="search-content-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested results are returned.|[SearchPageResponseSearchResult](#schemasearchpageresponsesearchresult)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the CQL query cannot be parsed.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to access<br>Confluence.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: search:confluence )
</aside>

## Search users

<a id="opIdsearchUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/search/user?cql=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/search/user`

Searches for users using user-specific queries from the
[Confluence Query Language (CQL)](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/advanced-searching-using-cql/).

Note that CQL input queries submitted through the `/wiki/rest/api/search/user` endpoint only support user-specific fields like `user`, `user.fullname`, `user.accountid`, and `user.userkey`.

Note that some user fields may be set to null depending on the user's privacy settings.
These are: email, profilePicture, displayName, and timeZone.

<h3 id="search-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cql|query|string|true|The CQL query to be used for the search. See<br>[Advanced Searching using CQL](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/advanced-searching-using-cql/)<br>for instructions on how to build a CQL query.<br><br>Example queries:<br>          cql=type=user will return up to 10k users<br>          cql=user="1234" will return user with accountId "1234"<br>          You can also use IN, NOT IN, != operators<br>          cql=user IN ("12", "34") will return users with accountids "12" and "34"<br>          cql=user.fullname~jo will return users with nickname/full name starting with "jo"<br>          cql=user.accountid="123" will return user with accountId "123"|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned users.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of user objects to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the user to expand.<br><br>- `operations` returns the operations for the user, which are used<br>when setting permissions.<br>- `personalSpace` returns the personal space of the user.|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|query|string|false|Filters users by permission type. Use `none` to default to licensed users, `externalCollaborator`<br>for external/guest users, and `all` to include all permission types.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|all|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|externalCollaborator|
|sitePermissionTypeFilter|none|

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-settings">Settings</h1>

## Get look and feel settings

<a id="opIdgetLookAndFeelSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/settings/lookandfeel \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/settings/lookandfeel`

Returns the look and feel settings for the site or a single space. This
includes attributes such as the color scheme, padding, and border radius.

The look and feel settings for a space can be inherited from the global
look and feel settings or provided by a theme.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
None

<h3 id="get-look-and-feel-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|query|string|false|The key of the space for which the look and feel settings will be<br>returned. If this is not set, only the global look and feel settings<br>are returned.|

</aside>

## Select look and feel settings

<a id="opIdupdateLookAndFeel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/settings/lookandfeel \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "spaceKey": "string",
    "lookAndFeelType": "global"
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/settings/lookandfeel`

Sets the look and feel settings to the default (global) settings, the
custom settings, or the current theme's settings for a space.
The custom and theme settings can only be selected if there is already
a theme set for a space. Note, the default space settings are inherited
from the current global settings.

**[Permissions](https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/what-are-confluences-roles/) required**:
[`manage/look-and-feel`](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) permission for the space.

**Note:** To find the display name for each permission ID, call the [Get available space permissions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) API.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "spaceKey": "string",
  "lookAndFeelType": "global"
}
```

<h3 id="select-look-and-feel-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LookAndFeelSelection](#schemalookandfeelselection)|true|The look and feel type to be set.|
|» spaceKey|body|string|true|The key of the space for which the look and feel settings will be<br>set.|
|» lookAndFeelType|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» lookAndFeelType|global|
|» lookAndFeelType|custom|
|» lookAndFeelType|theme|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "spaceKey": "string",
  "lookAndFeelType": "global"
}
```

<h3 id="select-look-and-feel-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the look and feel settings were set.|[LookAndFeelSelection](#schemalookandfeelselection)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- `spaceKey` is invalid.<br>- `lookAndFeelType` is invalid.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user doesn't have permission to edit the<br>look and feel settings.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if there is no space with the given `spaceKey`.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if `lookAndFeelType` is set to 'custom' or 'theme',<br>and a theme is not currently set for the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: manage:confluence-configuration )
</aside>

`POST /wiki/rest/api/settings/lookandfeel/custom`

Updates the look and feel settings for the site or for a single space.
If custom settings exist, they are updated. If no custom settings exist,
then a set of custom settings is created.

Note, if a theme is selected for a space, the space look and feel settings
are provided by the theme and cannot be overridden.

**[Permissions](https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/what-are-confluences-roles/) required**:

- If `spaceKey` is specified, [`manage/look-and-feel`](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) permission for the space.
- If `spaceKey` is omitted, 'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

**Note:** To find the display name for each permission ID, call the [Get available space permissions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) API.

## Reset look and feel settings

<a id="opIdresetLookAndFeelSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/settings/lookandfeel/custom \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/settings/lookandfeel/custom`

Resets the custom look and feel settings for the site or a single space.
This changes the values of the custom settings to be the same as the
default settings. It does not change which settings (default or custom)
are selected. Note, the default space settings are inherited from the
current global settings.

**[Permissions](https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/what-are-confluences-roles/) required**:

- If `spaceKey` is specified, [`manage/look-and-feel`](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) permission for the space.
- If `spaceKey` is omitted, 'Confluence Administrator' global permission.

**Note:** To find the display name for each permission ID, call the [Get available space permissions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) API.

<h3 id="reset-look-and-feel-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|query|string|false|The key of the space for which the look and feel settings will be<br>reset. If this is not set, the global look and feel settings will<br>be reset.|

<h3 id="reset-look-and-feel-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the look and feel settings have been reset.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if `spaceKey` is invalid.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user doesn't have permission to reset the<br>look and feel.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if there is no space with the given `spaceKey`.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: manage:confluence-configuration )
</aside>

## Get system info

<a id="opIdgetSystemInfo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/settings/systemInfo \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/settings/systemInfo`

Returns the system information for the Confluence Cloud tenant. This
information is used by Atlassian.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "cloudId": "string",
  "commitHash": "string",
  "baseUrl": "string",
  "fallbackBaseUrl": "string",
  "edition": "string",
  "siteTitle": "string",
  "defaultLocale": "string",
  "defaultTimeZone": "string",
  "microsPerimeter": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-system-info-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the system information for the Confluence Cloud tenant<br>is returned.|[SystemInfoEntity](#schemasysteminfoentity)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when the user does not have permission to view the system<br>information.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: manage:confluence-configuration )
</aside>

`POST /wiki/rest/api/space`

Creates a new space. Note, currently you cannot set space labels when
creating a space.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Create Space(s)' global permission.

<h3 id="create-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SpaceCreate](#schemaspacecreate)|true|The space to be created.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new space.|
|» key|body|string|false|The key for the new space. Format: See [Space<br>keys](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/lqNMMQ). If `alias` is not provided, this is required.|
|» alias|body|string|false|This field will be used as the new identifier for the space in confluence page URLs.<br>If the property is not provided the alias will be the provided key.<br>This property is experimental and may be changed or removed in the future.|
|» description|body|[SpaceDescriptionCreate](#schemaspacedescriptioncreate)|false|The description of the new/updated space. Note, only the 'plain' representation<br>can be used for the description when creating or updating a space.|
|» permissions|body|[[SpacePermissionCreate](#schemaspacepermissioncreate)]|false|The permissions for the new space. If no permissions are provided, the<br>[Confluence default space permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/UAgzKw#CreateaSpace-Spacepermissions)<br>are applied. Note that if permissions are provided, the space is<br>created with only the provided set of permissions, not<br>including the default space permissions. Space permissions<br>can be modified after creation using the space permissions<br>endpoints, and a private space can be created using the<br>create private space endpoint.|

## Create private space

<a id="opIdcreatePrivateSpace"></a>

`POST /wiki/rest/api/space/_private`

Creates a new space that is only visible to the creator. This method is
the same as the [Create space](#api-space-post) method with permissions
set to the current user only. Note, currently you cannot set space
labels when creating a space.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Create Space(s)' global permission.

## Update space

<a id="opIdupdateSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": {
      "plain": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "string"
      }
    },
    "homepage": {},
    "type": "string",
    "status": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}`

Updates the name, description, or homepage of a space.

-   For security reasons, permissions cannot be updated via the API and
must be changed via the user interface instead.
-   Currently you cannot set space labels when updating a space.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": {
    "plain": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "string"
    }
  },
  "homepage": {},
  "type": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to update.|
|body|body|[SpaceUpdate](#schemaspaceupdate)|true|The updated space.|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The updated name of the space.|
|» description|body|[SpaceDescriptionCreate](#schemaspacedescriptioncreate)|false|The description of the new/updated space. Note, only the 'plain' representation<br>can be used for the description when creating or updating a space.|
|» homepage|body|object \| null|false|The updated homepage for this space|
|» type|body|string|false|The updated type for this space.|
|» status|body|string \| null|false|The updated status for this space.|

## Delete space

<a id="opIddeleteSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}`

Permanently deletes a space without sending it to the trash. Note, the space will be deleted in a long running task.
Therefore, the space may not be deleted yet when this method has
returned. Clients should poll the status link that is returned in the
response until the task completes.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

<h3 id="delete-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to delete.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "ari": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "links": {
    "status": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Returns a pointer to the status of the space deletion task.|[LongTask](#schemalongtask)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if any of the following is true:<br><br>- There is no space with the given key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to delete the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-space )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-space-permissions">Space permissions</h1>

## Add new permission to space

<a id="opIdaddPermissionToSpace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/permission \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "subject": {
      "type": "user",
      "identifier": "string"
    },
    "operation": {
      "key": "administer",
      "target": "page"
    },
    "_links": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    }
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/permission`

Adds new permission to space.

If the permission to be added is a group permission, the group can be identified
by its group name or group id.

Note: Apps cannot access this REST resource - including when utilizing user impersonation.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subject": {
    "type": "user",
    "identifier": "string"
  },
  "operation": {
    "key": "administer",
    "target": "page"
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-new-permission-to-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to be queried for its content.|
|body|body|[SpacePermissionRequest](#schemaspacepermissionrequest)|true|The permission to be created.|
|» subject|body|[PermissionSubject](#schemapermissionsubject)|true|The user or group that the permission applies to.|
|» operation|body|object|true|none|
|» » key|body|string|true|none|
|» » target|body|string|true|The space or content type that the operation applies to.|
|» _links|body|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » key|administer|
|» » key|archive|
|» » key|copy|
|» » key|create|
|» » key|delete|
|» » key|export|
|» » key|move|
|» » key|purge|
|» » key|purge_version|
|» » key|read|
|» » key|restore|
|» » key|restrict_content|
|» » key|update|
|» » key|use|
|» » target|page|
|» » target|blogpost|
|» » target|comment|
|» » target|attachment|
|» » target|space|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "subject": {
    "type": "user",
    "identifier": "string"
  },
  "operation": {
    "key": "administer",
    "target": "page"
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-new-permission-to-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested content is returned.|[SpacePermissionV2](#schemaspacepermissionv2)|
|400|Bad Request|Used for various errors. Such as:<br>- Permission already exists for the given user or group.<br>- 'read space' permission doesn't exist for the given user or group.<br>- No group found with the given groupName or groupId|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user isn't authorized.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if any of the following is true:<br>- There is no space with the given key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:space.permission:confluence write:space.permission:confluence )
</aside>

## Add new custom content permission to space

<a id="opIdaddCustomContentPermissions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/permission/custom-content \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "subject": {
      "type": "user",
      "identifier": "string"
    },
    "operations": [
      {
        "key": "read",
        "target": "string",
        "access": true
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/permission/custom-content`

Adds new custom content permission to space.

If the permission to be added is a group permission, the group can be identified
by its group name or group id.

Note: Only apps can access this REST resource and only make changes to the respective app permissions.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subject": {
    "type": "user",
    "identifier": "string"
  },
  "operations": [
    {
      "key": "read",
      "target": "string",
      "access": true
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-new-custom-content-permission-to-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to be queried for its content.|
|body|body|[SpacePermissionCustomContent](#schemaspacepermissioncustomcontent)|true|The permissions to be created.|
|» subject|body|[PermissionSubject](#schemapermissionsubject)|true|The user or group that the permission applies to.|
|» operations|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » key|body|string|true|The operation type|
|» » target|body|string|true|The custom content type|
|» » access|body|boolean|true|Grant or restrict access|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » key|read|
|» » key|create|
|» » key|delete|

<h3 id="add-new-custom-content-permission-to-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested content is returned.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Used for various errors. Such as:<br>- Permission already exists for the given user or group.<br>- 'read space' permission doesn't exist for the given user or group.<br>- No group found with the given groupName or groupId|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user isn't authorized.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if any of the following is true:<br>- There is no space with the given key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:space.permission:confluence write:space.permission:confluence )
</aside>

## Remove a space permission

<a id="opIdremovePermission"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/permission/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/permission/{id}`

Removes a space permission. Note that removing Read Space permission for a user or group will remove all
the space permissions for that user or group.

Note: Apps cannot access this REST resource - including when utilizing user impersonation.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

<h3 id="remove-a-space-permission-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to be queried for its content.|
|id|path|integer|true|Id of the permission to be deleted.|

<h3 id="remove-a-space-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Permission successfully removed.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Used for various errors. Such as:<br>- All of the admin permissions cannot be removed from a space.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user isn't authorized.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if any of the following is true:<br>- There is no permission with the given id.<br>- There is no space with the given key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:space.permission:confluence )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-space-settings">Space settings</h1>

## Get space settings

<a id="opIdgetSpaceSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/settings`

Returns the settings of a space.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space.

<h3 id="get-space-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to be queried for its settings.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "routeOverrideEnabled": true,
  "editor": {
    "page": "string",
    "blogpost": "string",
    "default": "string"
  },
  "contentMode": "standard",
  "spaceKey": "string",
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-space-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the space settings are returned.|[SpaceSettings](#schemaspacesettings)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no space with the given key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-space.summary )
</aside>

## Update space settings

<a id="opIdupdateSpaceSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "routeOverrideEnabled": true,
    "contentMode": "standard"
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/settings`

Updates the settings for a space.

**[Permissions](https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/what-are-confluences-roles/) required**:
[`manage/space`](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) permission for the space.

**Note:** To find the display name for each permission ID, call the [Get available space permissions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) API.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "routeOverrideEnabled": true,
  "contentMode": "standard"
}
```

<h3 id="update-space-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space whose settings will be updated.|
|body|body|[SpaceSettingsUpdate](#schemaspacesettingsupdate)|true|The space settings to update.|
|» routeOverrideEnabled|body|boolean|false|Defines whether an override for the space home should be used. This is<br>used in conjunction with a space theme provided by an app. For<br>example, if this property is set to true, a theme can display a page<br>other than the space homepage when users visit the root URL for a<br>space. This property allows apps to provide content-only theming<br>without overriding the space home.|
|» contentMode|body|string \| null|false|The content rendering mode for the space. Controls spacing and typography<br>in the editor and renderer. Valid values are "standard" and "compact".<br>When set to "compact", content is rendered more densely with smaller<br>spacing and typography.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» contentMode|standard|
|» contentMode|compact|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "routeOverrideEnabled": true,
  "editor": {
    "page": "string",
    "blogpost": "string",
    "default": "string"
  },
  "contentMode": "standard",
  "spaceKey": "string",
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-space-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if space settings are updated.|[SpaceSettings](#schemaspacesettings)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no space with the given key.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to update the space.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-space )
</aside>

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/template`

Updates a content template. Note, blueprint templates cannot be updated
via the REST API.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:

global permission to update a global template.

<h3 id="update-content-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ContentTemplateUpdate](#schemacontenttemplateupdate)|true|The updated content template.|
|» templateId|body|string|true|The ID of the template being updated.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the template. Set to the current `name` if this field is<br>not being updated.|
|» templateType|body|string|true|The type of the template. Set to `page`.|
|» body|body|[ContentTemplateBodyCreate](#schemacontenttemplatebodycreate)|true|The body of the new content. Does not apply to attachments.<br>Only one body format should be specified as the property for<br>this object, e.g. `storage`.<br><br>Note, `editor2` format is used by Atlassian only. `anonymous_export_view` is<br>the same as `export_view` format but only content viewable by an anonymous<br>user is included.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the template.|
|» labels|body|[[Label](#schemalabel)]|false|Labels for the template.|
|» space|body|object \| null|false|The key for the space of the template. Required if the template is a<br>space template. Set this to the current `space.key`.|

<h3 id="update-content-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the template is updated.|[ContentTemplate](#schemacontenttemplate)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if template name is null or an empty string.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to update the<br>template or if the template doesn't exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Create content template

<a id="opIdcreateContentTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/template \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "templateType": "string",
    "body": {
      "view": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "export_view": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "styled_view": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "storage": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "editor": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "editor2": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "wiki": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "atlas_doc_format": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      },
      "anonymous_export_view": {
        "value": "string",
        "representation": "view"
      }
    },
    "description": "string",
    "labels": [
      {
        "prefix": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "id": "string",
        "label": "string"
      }
    ],
    "space": {
      "key": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/template`

Creates a new content template. Note, blueprint templates cannot be created via the REST API.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space to create a space template or 'Confluence Administrator'
global permission to create a global template.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "templateType": "string",
  "body": {
    "view": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "export_view": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "styled_view": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "storage": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "editor": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "editor2": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "wiki": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "atlas_doc_format": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    },
    "anonymous_export_view": {
      "value": "string",
      "representation": "view"
    }
  },
  "description": "string",
  "labels": [
    {
      "prefix": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "label": "string"
    }
  ],
  "space": {
    "key": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-content-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ContentTemplateCreate](#schemacontenttemplatecreate)|true|The content template to be created.<br>The content body must be in 'storage' format.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new template.|
|» templateType|body|string|true|The type of the new template. Set to `page`.|
|» body|body|[ContentTemplateBodyCreate](#schemacontenttemplatebodycreate)|true|The body of the new content. Does not apply to attachments.<br>Only one body format should be specified as the property for<br>this object, e.g. `storage`.<br><br>Note, `editor2` format is used by Atlassian only. `anonymous_export_view` is<br>the same as `export_view` format but only content viewable by an anonymous<br>user is included.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the new template.|
|» labels|body|[[Label](#schemalabel)]|false|Labels for the new template.|
|» space|body|object \| null|false|The key for the space of the new template. Only applies to space templates.<br>If the spaceKey is not specified, the template will be created as a global<br>template.|
|» » key|body|string|true|none|
