<h3 id="create-content-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the template is created.|[ContentTemplate](#schemacontenttemplate)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if template name is null or an empty string.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to create the<br>template.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

## Get blueprint templates

<a id="opIdgetBlueprintTemplates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/template/blueprint \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/template/blueprint`

Returns all templates provided by blueprints. Use this method to retrieve
all global blueprint templates or all blueprint templates in a space.

Note, all global blueprints are inherited by each space. Space blueprints
can be customised without affecting the global blueprints.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space to view blueprints for the space and permission
to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission) to view global blueprints.

<h3 id="get-blueprint-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|query|string|false|The key of the space to be queried for templates. If the `spaceKey`<br>is not specified, global blueprint templates will be returned.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned templates.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of templates to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the template<br>to expand.<br><br>- `body` or `body.storage` returns the content of the template in storage format.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|body|
|expand|body.storage|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/template/page \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/template/page`

Returns all content templates. Use this method to retrieve all global
content templates or all content templates in a space.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space to view space templates and permission to
access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission) to view global templates.

<h3 id="get-content-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|query|string|false|The key of the space to be queried for templates. If the `spaceKey`<br>is not specified, global templates will be returned.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned templates.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of templates to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the template<br>to expand.<br><br>- `body` or `body.storage` returns the content of the template in storage format.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|body|
|expand|body.storage|

<h3 id="get-content-templates-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested templates are returned.|[ContentTemplateArray](#schemacontenttemplatearray)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to view the<br>content templates.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Get content template

<a id="opIdgetContentTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/template/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/template/{contentTemplateId}`

Returns a content template. This includes information about template,
like the name, the space or blueprint that the template is in, the body
of the template, and more.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'View' permission for the space to view space templates and permission to
access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission) to view global templates.

<h3 id="get-content-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentTemplateId|path|string|true|The ID of the content template to be returned.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the template<br>to expand.<br><br>- `body` or `body.storage` returns the content of the template in storage format.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|body|
|expand|body.storage|

<h3 id="get-content-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested template is returned.|[ContentTemplate](#schemacontenttemplate)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no template with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to view the template.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-content.summary )
</aside>

## Remove template

<a id="opIdremoveTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/template/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/template/{contentTemplateId}`

Deletes a template. This results in different actions depending on the
type of template:

- If the template is a content template, it is deleted.
- If the template is a modified space-level blueprint template, it reverts
to the template inherited from the global-level blueprint template.
- If the template is a modified global-level blueprint template, it reverts
to the default global-level blueprint template.

 Note, unmodified blueprint templates cannot be deleted.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
        'Admin' permission for the space to delete a space template or 'Confluence Administrator'
        global permission to delete a global template.

<h3 id="remove-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentTemplateId|path|string|true|The ID of the template to be deleted.|

<h3 id="remove-template-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the template has been successfully been deleted.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no template with the given ID.<br>- The calling user does not have permission to delete the template.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-content )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-themes">Themes</h1>

## Get themes

<a id="opIdgetThemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/settings/theme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/settings/theme`

Returns all themes, not including the default theme.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**: None

<h3 id="get-themes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned themes.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of themes to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "themeKey": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "icon": {
        "path": "string",
        "width": 0,
        "height": 0,
        "isDefault": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-themes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested themes are returned.|[ThemeArray](#schemathemearray)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: manage:confluence-configuration )
</aside>

## Get global theme

<a id="opIdgetGlobalTheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/settings/theme/selected \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/settings/theme/selected`

Returns the globally assigned theme.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**: None

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "themeKey": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "icon": {
    "path": "string",
    "width": 0,
    "height": 0,
    "isDefault": true
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-global-theme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the global theme is returned.|[Theme](#schematheme)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if Confluence does not have a global theme assigned, i.e.<br>the default theme is used.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: manage:confluence-configuration )
</aside>

## Get theme

<a id="opIdgetTheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/settings/theme/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/settings/theme/{themeKey}`

Returns a theme. This includes information about the theme name,
description, and icon.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**: None

<h3 id="get-theme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|themeKey|path|string|true|The key of the theme to be returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "themeKey": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "icon": {
    "path": "string",
    "width": 0,
    "height": 0,
    "isDefault": true
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-theme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested theme is returned.|[Theme](#schematheme)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if there is no theme with the given key.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: manage:confluence-configuration )
</aside>

## Get space theme

<a id="opIdgetSpaceTheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/theme \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/theme`

Returns the theme selected for a space, if one is set. If no space
theme is set, this means that the space is inheriting the global look
and feel settings.

**[Permissions required](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw)**: ‘View’ permission for the space.

<h3 id="get-space-theme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to be queried for its theme.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "themeKey": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "icon": {
    "path": "string",
    "width": 0,
    "height": 0,
    "isDefault": true
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-space-theme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested theme is returned.|[Theme](#schematheme)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if any of the following is true:<br><br>- There is no space with the given key.<br>- The space does not have a theme assigned to it.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:confluence-space.summary )
</aside>

## Set space theme

<a id="opIdsetSpaceTheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/theme \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "themeKey": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/theme`

Sets the theme for a space. Note, if you want to reset the space theme to
the default Confluence theme, use the 'Reset space theme' method instead
of this method.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "themeKey": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="set-space-theme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to set the theme for.|
|body|body|[ThemeUpdate](#schemathemeupdate)|true|none|
|» themeKey|body|string|true|The key of the theme to be set as the space theme.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "themeKey": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "icon": {
    "path": "string",
    "width": 0,
    "height": 0,
    "isDefault": true
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="set-space-theme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the theme was set for the space.|[Theme](#schematheme)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the theme key is invalid.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if there is no space with the given key.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-space )
</aside>

## Reset space theme

<a id="opIdresetSpaceTheme"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/space/string/theme \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /wiki/rest/api/space/{spaceKey}/theme`

Resets the space theme. This means that the space will inherit the
global look and feel settings

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
'Admin' permission for the space.

<h3 id="reset-space-theme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spaceKey|path|string|true|The key of the space to reset the theme for.|

<h3 id="reset-space-theme-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the theme was reset for the space.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if there is no space with the given key.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:confluence-space )
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-users">Users</h1>

## Get user

<a id="opIdgetUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user?accountId=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/user`

Returns a user. This includes information about the user, such as the
display name, account ID, profile picture, and more. The information returned may be
restricted by the user's profile visibility settings.

**Note:** to add, edit, or delete users in your organization, see the
[user management REST API](/cloud/admin/user-management/about/).

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="get-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|query|string|true|The account ID of the user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products.<br>For example, `384093:32b4d9w0-f6a5-3535-11a3-9c8c88d10192`.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|A multi-value parameter indicating which properties of the user to<br>expand.<br><br>  - `operations` returns the operations that the user is allowed to do.<br>  - `personalSpace` returns the user's personal space, if it exists.<br>  - `isExternalCollaborator`(@deprecated) see `isGuest` in response to find out whether the user is a guest.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|operations|
|expand|personalSpace|
|expand|isExternalCollaborator|

```json
  "type": "known",

    "height": 0,

      "location": "string"
    },

      "email": "string"

    "operations": "string",
    "details": "string",
    "personalSpace": "string"
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested user is returned.|[User](#schemauser)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the calling user does not have permission to view users.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if a user with the given accountId does not exist.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

## Get user email address

<a id="opIdgetPrivacyUnsafeUserEmail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/email?accountId=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/user/email`

Returns a user's email address regardless of the user’s profile visibility settings. For Connect apps, this API is only available to apps approved by
Atlassian, according to these [guidelines](https://community.developer.atlassian.com/t/guidelines-for-requesting-access-to-email-address/27603).
For Forge apps, this API only supports access via asApp() requests.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="get-user-email-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|query|string|true|The account ID of the user, which uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian products.<br>For example, `384093:32b4d9w0-f6a5-3535-11a3-9c8c88d10192`. Required.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accountId": "string",
  "email": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-user-email-address-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested user's email is returned.|[AccountIdEmailRecord](#schemaaccountidemailrecord)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the calling app is not approved to use this API.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing<br>from the request.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if a user with the given accountId does not exist.|None|
|501|Not Implemented|Indicates that the API is not currently enabled.|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="the-confluence-cloud-rest-api-user-properties">User properties</h1>

## Get user properties

<a id="opIdgetUserProperties"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/string/property \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/user/{userId}/property`

Returns the properties for a user as list of property keys. For more information
about user properties, see [Confluence entity properties](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/confluence-entity-properties/).
`Note`, these properties stored against a user are on a Confluence site level and not space/content level.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="get-user-properties-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The account ID of the user to be queried for its properties.|
|start|query|integer(int32)|false|The starting index of the returned properties.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of properties to return per page.<br>Note, this may be restricted by fixed system limits.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "key": "string"
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "size": 0,
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-user-properties-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested properties are returned.|[UserPropertyKeyArray](#schemauserpropertykeyarray)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if request has malformed syntax or userId is not a valid user id.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the correct permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if there is no user with the given user ID.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:user.property:confluence )
</aside>

## Get user property

<a id="opIdgetUserProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/string/property/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /wiki/rest/api/user/{userId}/property/{key}`

Returns the property corresponding to `key` for a user. For more information
about user properties, see [Confluence entity properties](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/confluence-entity-properties/).
`Note`, these properties stored against a user are on a Confluence site level and not space/content level.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

<h3 id="get-user-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The account ID of the user to be queried for its properties.|
|key|path|string|true|The key of the user property.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key": "string",
  "value": {},
  "id": "string",
  "lastModifiedDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "createdDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-user-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returned if the requested properties are returned.|[UserProperty](#schemauserproperty)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- The key is too long.<br>- Request has malformed syntax or userId is not a valid user id.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the correct permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no user with the given user ID<br>- There is no user property with the given key|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: read:user.property:confluence )
</aside>

## Update user property

<a id="opIdupdateUserProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/string/property/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "value": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /wiki/rest/api/user/{userId}/property/{key}`

Updates a property for the given user. Note, you cannot update the key of a user property, only the value.
For more information about user properties, see
[Confluence entity properties](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/confluence-entity-properties/).
`Note`, these properties stored against a user are on a Confluence site level and not space/content level.

**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-user-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The account ID of the user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian<br>products. For example, 384093:32b4d9w0-f6a5-3535-11a3-9c8c88d10192|
|key|path|string|true|The key of the user property.|
|body|body|[UserPropertyUpdate](#schemauserpropertyupdate)|true|The user property to be updated.|
|» value|body|object|true|The value of the user property.|

<h3 id="update-user-property-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Returned if the user property is updated.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- The key is too long.<br>- The value is empty.<br>- The value is too long.<br>- Request has malformed syntax or userId is not a valid user id.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the correct permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if;<br><br>- There is no user property with the given key.<br>- There is no user with the given user id.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:user.property:confluence )
</aside>

## Create user property by key

<a id="opIdcreateUserProperty"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/wiki/rest/api/user/string/property/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "value": {}
  }'
```

`POST /wiki/rest/api/user/{userId}/property/{key}`

Creates a property for a user. For more information  about user properties, see [Confluence entity properties]
(https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/confluence-entity-properties/).
`Note`, these properties stored against a user are on a Confluence site level and not space/content level.

`Note:` the number of properties which could be created per app in a tenant for each user might be
restricted by fixed system limits.
**[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**:
Permission to access the Confluence site ('Can use' global permission).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "value": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-user-property-by-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|The account ID of the user. The accountId uniquely identifies the user across all Atlassian<br>products. For example, 384093:32b4d9w0-f6a5-3535-11a3-9c8c88d10192|
|key|path|string|true|The key of the user property.|
|body|body|[UserPropertyCreate](#schemauserpropertycreate)|true|The user property to be created.|
|» value|body|object|true|The value of the user property.|

<h3 id="create-user-property-by-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returned if the user property is created.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if;<br><br>- The key is too long.<br>- The value is empty.<br>- The value is too long.<br>- Request has malformed syntax or userId is not a valid user id.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned if the authentication credentials are incorrect or missing from the request.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have the correct permissions.|None|
|404|Not Found|Returned if there is no user with the given user id.|None|
|409|Conflict|Returned if the key already exists for the user.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth, oAuthDefinitions ( Scopes: write:user.property:confluence )
</aside>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|author|object|false|none|The user that actioned the event. If `author` is not specified, then all<br>`author` properties will be set to null/empty, except for `type` which<br>will be set to 'user'.|
|remoteAddress|string|true|none|The IP address of the computer where the event was initiated from.|
|creationDate|integer(int64)|false|none|The creation date-time of the audit record, as a timestamp. This is converted<br>to a date-time display in the Confluence UI. If the `creationDate` is not<br>specified, then it will be set to the timestamp for the current date-time.|
|summary|string|false|none|The summary of the event, which is displayed in the 'Change' column on<br>the audit log in the Confluence UI.|
|description|string|false|none|A long description of the event, which is displayed in the 'Description'<br>field on the audit log in the Confluence UI.|
|category|string|false|none|The category of the event, which is displayed in the 'Event type' column<br>on the audit log in the Confluence UI.|
|sysAdmin|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the event was actioned by a system administrator.|
|affectedObject|[AffectedObject](#schemaaffectedobject)|false|none|none|
|changedValues|[[ChangedValue](#schemachangedvalue)]|false|none|The values that were changed in the event.|
|associatedObjects|[[AffectedObject](#schemaaffectedobject)]|false|none|Objects that were associated with the event. For example, if the event<br>was a space permission change then the associated object would be the<br>space.|

|body|[ContentTemplateBody](#schemacontenttemplatebody)|false|none|The body of the new content. Does not apply to attachments.<br>Only one body format should be specified as the property for<br>this object, e.g. `storage`.<br><br>Note, `editor2` format is used by Atlassian only. `anonymous_export_view` is<br>the same as `export_view` format but only content viewable by an anonymous<br>user is included.|
|_expandable|object|false|none|none|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|true|none|none|


Base object for all content types.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|Can be "page", "blogpost", "attachment" or "content"|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|title|string|false|none|none|
|space|[Space](#schemaspace)|false|none|none|
|history|[ContentHistory](#schemacontenthistory)|false|none|none|
|version|[Version](#schemaversion)|false|none|none|
|ancestors|[[Content](#schemacontent)]|false|none|none|
|operations|[[OperationCheckResult](#schemaoperationcheckresult)]|false|none|none|
|children|[ContentChildren](#schemacontentchildren)|false|none|none|
|childTypes|[ContentChildType](#schemacontentchildtype)|false|none|Shows whether a piece of content has attachments, comments, or child pages/whiteboards.<br>Note, this doesn't actually contain the child objects.|
|descendants|[ContentChildren](#schemacontentchildren)|false|none|none|
|container|[Container](#schemacontainer)|false|none|Container for content. This can be either a space (containing a page or blogpost)<br>or a page/blog post (containing an attachment or comment)|
|body|object|false|none|none|
|restrictions|object|false|none|none|
|metadata|[ContentMetadata](#schemacontentmetadata)|false|none|Metadata object for page, blogpost, comment content|
|macroRenderedOutput|object|false|none|none|
|extensions|object|false|none|none|
|_expandable|object|false|none|none|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|false|none|none|

Representation of a blogpost (content)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|Can be "page", "blogpost", "attachment" or "content"|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|title|string|false|none|none|
|space|[Space](#schemaspace)|false|none|none|
|history|[ContentHistory](#schemacontenthistory)|false|none|none|
|version|[Version](#schemaversion)|false|none|none|
|ancestors|[[Content](#schemacontent)]|false|none|none|
|operations|[[OperationCheckResult](#schemaoperationcheckresult)]|false|none|none|
|children|[ContentChildren](#schemacontentchildren)|false|none|none|
|childTypes|[ContentChildType](#schemacontentchildtype)|false|none|Shows whether a piece of content has attachments, comments, or child pages/whiteboards.<br>Note, this doesn't actually contain the child objects.|
|descendants|[ContentChildren](#schemacontentchildren)|false|none|none|
|container|[Container](#schemacontainer)|false|none|Container for content. This can be either a space (containing a page or blogpost)<br>or a page/blog post (containing an attachment or comment)|
|body|object|false|none|none|
|restrictions|object|false|none|none|
|metadata|[ContentMetadata](#schemacontentmetadata)|true|none|Metadata object for page, blogpost, comment content|
|macroRenderedOutput|object|false|none|none|
|extensions|object|false|none|none|
|_expandable|object|false|none|none|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|true|none|none|
|metadata|[ContentMetadata](#schemacontentmetadata)|true|none|Metadata object for page, blogpost, comment content|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ContentBlueprintDraft">ContentBlueprintDraft</h2>

```json
{
  "version": {
    "number": 0
  },
  "title": "string",
  "type": "page",
  "status": "current",
  "space": {
    "key": "string"
  },
  "ancestors": [
    {
      "id": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|object|true|none|The version for the new content.|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the content. If you don't want to change the title,<br>set this to the current title of the draft.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of content. Set this to `page`.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the content. Set this to `current` or omit it altogether.|
|space|object|false|none|The space for the content.|
|ancestors|[object]|false|none|The new ancestor (i.e. parent page) for the content. If you have<br>specified an ancestor, you must also specify a `space` property<br>in the request body for the space that the ancestor is in.<br><br>Note, if you specify more than one ancestor, the last ID in the array<br>will be selected as the parent page for the content.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|page|
|status|current|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the draft content. Required when publishing a draft.|
|title|string \| null|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the new content. Custom content types defined by apps are also supported. eg. 'page', 'blogpost', 'comment' etc.|
|space|object \| null|false|none|The space that the content is being created in.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the new content.|
|container|object \| null|false|none|The container of the content. Required if type is `comment` or certain types of<br>custom content. If you are trying to create a comment that is a child of another comment,<br>specify the parent comment in the ancestors field, not in this field.|
|ancestors|[object]|false|none|The parent content of the new content.  If you are creating a top-level `page` or `comment`,<br>this can be left blank. If you are creating a child page, this is where the parent page id goes.<br>If you are creating a child comment, this is where the parent comment id goes. Only one parent<br>content id can be specified.|
|body|object|false|none|The body of the new content. Does not apply to attachments.<br>Only one body format should be specified as the property for<br>this object, e.g. `storage`.<br><br>Note, `editor2` format is used by Atlassian only. `anonymous_export_view` is<br>the same as `export_view` format but only content viewable by an anonymous<br>user is included.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|current|
|status|deleted|
|status|historical|
|status|draft|

```json
        }
```
```json
      ]
```

```json
        {
          "id": "string",
          "type": "group"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "content": {
    "id": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|operation|string|true|none|The operation to restrict. Include each operation at most once per request.|
|restrictions|object|true|none|At least one of `user` or `group` must be supplied. On PUT, a supplied list<br>replaces the existing list for this operation and subject type; an empty<br>list clears it. Omitted lists are preserved. On POST, supplied lists add<br>to existing restrictions and empty lists add nothing.|
|content|object|false|none|Optional content reference. If supplied, its ID must match the path parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|operation|read|
|operation|update|

<h2 id="tocS_ContentState">ContentState</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontentstate"></a>
<a id="schema_ContentState"></a>
<a id="tocScontentstate"></a>
<a id="tocscontentstate"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "color": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|none|identifier of content state. If 0, 1, or 2, this is a default space state|
|name|string|true|none|name of content state.|
|color|string|true|none|hex string representing color of state|

<h2 id="tocS_ContentStateRestInput">ContentStateRestInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontentstaterestinput"></a>
<a id="schema_ContentStateRestInput"></a>
<a id="tocScontentstaterestinput"></a>
<a id="tocscontentstaterestinput"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "color": "string",
  "id": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Name of content state. Maximum 20 characters.|
|color|string|false|none|Color of state. Must be in 6 digit hex form (#FFFFFF). The default colors offered in the UI are:<br> #ff7452 (red),<br> #2684ff (blue),<br> #ffc400 (yellow),<br> #57d9a3 (green), and<br> #8777d9 (purple)|
|id|integer(int64)|false|none|id of state. This can be 0,1, or 2 if you wish to specify a default space state.|

<h2 id="tocS_ContentStateResponse">ContentStateResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontentstateresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_ContentStateResponse"></a>
<a id="tocScontentstateresponse"></a>
<a id="tocscontentstateresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "contentState": {
    "id": 0,
    "name": "string",
    "color": "string"
  },
  "lastUpdated": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentState|[ContentState](#schemacontentstate)|false|none|Null or content state|
|lastUpdated|string|false|none|Timestamp of last publish event where content state changed|

<h2 id="tocS_ContentStateSettings">ContentStateSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontentstatesettings"></a>
<a id="schema_ContentStateSettings"></a>
<a id="tocScontentstatesettings"></a>
<a id="tocscontentstatesettings"></a>

```json
{
  "contentStatesAllowed": true,
  "customContentStatesAllowed": true,
  "spaceContentStatesAllowed": true,
  "spaceContentStates": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "name": "string",
      "color": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contentStatesAllowed|boolean|true|none|Whether users can place any content states on content|
|customContentStatesAllowed|boolean|true|none|Whether users can place their custom states on content|
|spaceContentStatesAllowed|boolean|true|none|Whether users can place space suggested states on content|
|spaceContentStates|[[ContentState](#schemacontentstate)]|false|none|space suggested content states that users can choose from|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|templateId|string|true|none|none|

|editorVersion|string|false|none|none|
|body|[ContentTemplateBody](#schemacontenttemplatebody)|false|none|The body of the new content. Does not apply to attachments.<br>Only one body format should be specified as the property for<br>this object, e.g. `storage`.<br><br>Note, `editor2` format is used by Atlassian only. `anonymous_export_view` is<br>the same as `export_view` format but only content viewable by an anonymous<br>user is included.|
|_expandable|object|false|none|none|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|true|none|none|


This object is used to create content templates.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the new template.|
|templateType|string|true|none|The type of the new template. Set to `page`.|
|body|[ContentTemplateBodyCreate](#schemacontenttemplatebodycreate)|true|none|The body of the new content. Does not apply to attachments.<br>Only one body format should be specified as the property for<br>this object, e.g. `storage`.<br><br>Note, `editor2` format is used by Atlassian only. `anonymous_export_view` is<br>the same as `export_view` format but only content viewable by an anonymous<br>user is included.|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the new template.|
|labels|[[Label](#schemalabel)]|false|none|Labels for the new template.|
|space|object \| null|false|none|The key for the space of the new template. Only applies to space templates.<br>If the spaceKey is not specified, the template will be created as a global<br>template.|

user is included.

Set this to the current version number incremented by one, unless you are changing the status to 'draft' which must have a version number of 1.<br><br>To get the current version number, use [Get content by ID](#api-content-id-get) and retrieve `version.number`.|
|title|string \| null|false|none|The updated title of the content. If you are updating a non-draft `page` or `blogpost`, title is required. If you are not changing the title, set this field to the the current title.|
|type|string \| null|true|none|The type of content. Set this to the current type of the content. For example, - page - blogpost - comment - attachment|
|status|string|false|none|The updated status of the content. Note, if you change the status of a page from<br>'current' to 'draft' and it has an existing draft, the existing draft will be deleted<br>in favor of the updated page.|
|ancestors|[object]|false|none|The new parent for the content. Only one parent content 'id' can be specified.|
|body|object|false|none|The updated body of the content. Does not apply to attachments.<br>If you are not sure how to generate these formats, you can create a page in the<br>Confluence application, retrieve the content using [Get content](#api-content-get),<br>and expand the desired content format, e.g. `expand=body.storage`.|

|status|trashed|

|status|draft|

<h2 id="tocS_ContentBodyConversionInput">ContentBodyConversionInput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontentbodyconversioninput"></a>
<a id="schema_ContentBodyConversionInput"></a>
<a id="tocScontentbodyconversioninput"></a>
<a id="tocscontentbodyconversioninput"></a>

```json
{
  "to": "string",
  "allowCache": false,
  "spaceKeyContext": "string",
  "contentIdContext": "string",
  "embeddedContentRender": "current",
  "expand": [
    "string"
  ],
  "body": {
    "value": "string",
    "representation": "view"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|to|string|true|none|The name of the target format for the content body conversion.|
|allowCache|boolean|false|none|Controls whether conversion results are cached and reused for identical requests.<br><br>- `false`: Each request creates a new conversion task, even if an identical request was made previously.<br>- `true`: Enables caching behavior for identical requests from the same user.<br>  - If no cached result exists, a new conversion task is created<br>  - If a cached result exists, the existing task is marked as RERUNNING and will complete with status COMPLETED<br>  - Returns the same task ID for identical requests, allowing you to retrieve the cached result|
|spaceKeyContext|string|false|none|The space key used for resolving embedded content (page includes, files, and links) in the content body. For example, if the source content contains the link `<ac:link><ri:page ri:content-title="Example page" /><ac:link>` and the `spaceKeyContext=TEST` parameter is provided, then the link will be converted into a link to the "Example page" page in the "TEST" space.|
|contentIdContext|string|false|none|The content ID used to find the space for resolving embedded content (page includes, files, and links) in the content body. For example, if the source content contains the link `<ac:link><ri:page ri:content-title="Example page" /><ac:link>` and the `contentIdContext=123` parameter is provided, then the link will be converted into a link to the "Example page" page in the same space that has the content with ID=123. Note that `spaceKeyContext` will be ignored if this parameter is provided.|
|embeddedContentRender|string|false|none|Mode used for rendering embedded content, such as attachments. - `current` renders the embedded content using the latest version. - `version-at-save` renders the embedded content using the version at the time of save.|
|expand|[string]|false|none|A multi-value, comma-separated parameter indicating which properties of the content to expand and populate. Expands are dependent<br>on the `to` conversion format and may be irrelevant for certain conversions (e.g. `macroRenderedOutput` is redundant when<br>converting to `view` format). <br><br>If rendering to `view` format, and the body content being converted includes arbitrary nested content (such as macros); then it is <br>necessary to include webresource expands in the request. Webresources for content body are the batched JS and CSS dependencies for<br>any nested dynamic content (i.e. macros).<br><br>- `embeddedContent` returns metadata for nested content (e.g. page included using page include macro)<br>- `mediaToken` returns JWT token for retrieving attachment data from Media API<br>- `macroRenderedOutput` additionally converts body to view format<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.js` returns all common JS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.uris.all` returns all common dependencies as static URLs<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.all` returns all common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.css` returns all common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.superbatch.tags.js` returns all common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.uris.js` returns JS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.css` returns CSS dependencies specific to conversion<br>- `webresource.uris.all` returns all dependencies specific to conversion     <br>- `webresource.tags.all` returns common JS dependencies as html `<script>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.css` returns common CSS dependencies as html `<style>` tags<br>- `webresource.tags.js` returns common dependencies as html `<script>` and `<style>` tags|
|body|[ContentBodyCreate](#schemacontentbodycreate)|true|none|This object is used when creating or updating content.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|embeddedContentRender|current|
|embeddedContentRender|version-at-save|

  - `parent_page`: page will be copied as a child of the specified parent page

  - `existing_page`: page will be copied and replace the specified page

<h2 id="tocS_LongTaskStatus">LongTaskStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalongtaskstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_LongTaskStatus"></a>
<a id="tocSlongtaskstatus"></a>
<a id="tocslongtaskstatus"></a>

```json
{
  "ari": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "name": {
    "key": "string",
    "args": [
      {}
    ]
  },
  "elapsedTime": 0,
  "percentageComplete": 0,
  "successful": true,
  "finished": true,
  "messages": [
    {
      "translation": "string",
      "args": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "status": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "translation": "string",
      "args": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "additionalDetails": {
    "destinationId": "string",
    "destinationUrl": "string",
    "totalPageNeedToCopy": 0,
    "additionalProperties": "string"
  }
}
```

Current status of a long running task

Status keys:

- `ERROR_UNKNOWN` - Generic error
- `ERROR_LOCK_FAILED` - Could not get the lock on destination space
- `ERROR_RELINK` - Error when relink pages/attachments
- `ERROR_COPY_PAGE` - Error while copying 1 page
- `WARN_RENAME_PAGE` - Warning page is rename during copy
- `WARN_IGNORE_COPY_PERMISSION` - Warning could not copy permission
- `WARN_IGNORE_COPY_ATTACHMENT` - Warning could not copy attachment
- `WARN_IGNORE_DELETE_PAGE` - Warning ignoring delete of a non agreed on page
- `STATUS_COPIED_PAGES` - Message total pages are copied
- `STATUS_COPYING_PAGES` - Message copy pages
- `STATUS_RELINK_PAGES` - Message relink pages/attachments
- `STATUS_DELETING_PAGES` - Message delete pages
- `STATUS_DELETED_PAGES` - Message total pages are deleted
- `STATUS_MOVING_PAGES` - Message move pages
- `WARN_IGNORE_VIEW_RESTRICTED` - Permission changed - view restricted
- `WARN_IGNORE_EDIT_RESTRICTED` - Permission changed - edit restricted
- `INITIALIZING_TASK` - Message when initializing task
- `UNKNOWN_STATUS` - Message when status is unknown

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ari|string|false|none|the ARI for the long task, based on its ID|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|name|object|true|none|none|
|elapsedTime|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|percentageComplete|integer(int32)|true|none|none|
|successful|boolean|true|none|none|
|finished|boolean|true|none|none|
|messages|[[Message](#schemamessage)]|true|none|none|
|status|string|false|none|none|
|errors|[[Message](#schemamessage)]|false|none|none|
|additionalDetails|object|false|none|none|

This is the request object used when creating a new space.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the new space.|
|key|string|false|none|The key for the new space. Format: See [Space<br>keys](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/lqNMMQ). If `alias` is not provided, this is required.|
|alias|string|false|none|This field will be used as the new identifier for the space in confluence page URLs.<br>If the property is not provided the alias will be the provided key.<br>This property is experimental and may be changed or removed in the future.|
|description|[SpaceDescriptionCreate](#schemaspacedescriptioncreate)|false|none|The description of the new/updated space. Note, only the 'plain' representation<br>can be used for the description when creating or updating a space.|
|permissions|[[SpacePermissionCreate](#schemaspacepermissioncreate)]|false|none|The permissions for the new space. If no permissions are provided, the<br>[Confluence default space permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/UAgzKw#CreateaSpace-Spacepermissions)<br>are applied. Note that if permissions are provided, the space is<br>created with only the provided set of permissions, not<br>including the default space permissions. Space permissions<br>can be modified after creation using the space permissions<br>endpoints, and a private space can be created using the<br>create private space endpoint.|

This object represents a permission for given space. Permissions consist of
at least one operation object with an accompanying subjects object.

The following combinations of `operation` and `targetType` values are
valid for the `operation` object:

  - 'create': 'page', 'blogpost', 'comment', 'attachment'
  - 'read': 'space'
  - 'delete': 'page', 'blogpost', 'comment', 'attachment'
  - 'export': 'space'
  - 'administer': 'space'

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|false|none|none|
|subjects|object|false|none|The users and/or groups that the permission applies to.|
|operation|[OperationCheckResult](#schemaoperationcheckresult)|true|none|An operation and the target entity that it applies to, e.g. create page.|
|anonymousAccess|boolean|true|none|Grant anonymous users permission to use the operation.|
|unlicensedAccess|boolean|true|none|Grants access to unlicensed users from JIRA Service Desk when used<br>with the 'read space' operation.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|routeOverrideEnabled|boolean|true|none|Defines whether an override for the space home should be used. This is<br>used in conjunction with a space theme provided by an app. For<br>example, if this property is set to true, a theme can display a page<br>other than the space homepage when users visit the root URL for a<br>space. This property allows apps to provide content-only theming<br>without overriding the space home.|
|editor|object|false|none|none|
|contentMode|string \| null|false|none|The content rendering mode for the space. Controls spacing and typography<br>in the editor and renderer. Valid values are "standard" and "compact".<br>When set to "compact", content is rendered more densely with smaller<br>spacing and typography.|
|spaceKey|string|false|none|none|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|true|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|contentMode|compact|

<h2 id="tocS_SpacePermissionV2">SpacePermissionV2</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaspacepermissionv2"></a>
<a id="schema_SpacePermissionV2"></a>
<a id="tocSspacepermissionv2"></a>
<a id="tocsspacepermissionv2"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "subject": {
    "type": "user",
    "identifier": "string"
  },
  "operation": {
    "key": "administer",
    "target": "page"
  },
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

This object represents a single space permission. Permissions consist of
at least one operation object with an accompanying subjects object.

The following combinations of `operation.key` and `operation.target` values are
valid for the `operation` object:
``` bash
'create': 'page', 'blogpost', 'comment', 'attachment'
'read': 'space'
'delete': 'page', 'blogpost', 'comment', 'attachment', 'space'
'export': 'space'
'administer': 'space'
'archive': 'page'
'restrict_content': 'space'
```

For example, to enable Delete Own permission, set the `operation` object to the following:
```
"operation": {
    "key": "delete",
    "target": "space"
}
```
To enable Add/Delete Restrictions permissions, set the `operation` object to the following:
```
"operation": {
    "key": "restrict_content",
    "target": "space"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer(int64)|true|none|none|
|subject|[PermissionSubject](#schemapermissionsubject)|true|none|The user or group that the permission applies to.|
|operation|object|true|none|none|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_PermissionCheckResponse">PermissionCheckResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapermissioncheckresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_PermissionCheckResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSpermissioncheckresponse"></a>
<a id="tocspermissioncheckresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "hasPermission": true,
  "errors": [
    {
      "translation": "string",
      "args": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "_links": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

This object represents the response for the content permission check API. If the user or group does not have
permissions, the following errors may be returned:

- Group does not have permission to the space
- Group does not have permission to the content
- User is not allowed to use Confluence
- User does not have permission to the space
- User does not have permission to the content
- Anonymous users are not allowed to use Confluence
- Anonymous user does not have permission to the space
- Anonymous user does not have permission to the content

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hasPermission|boolean|true|none|none|
|errors|[[Message](#schemamessage)]|false|none|none|
|_links|[GenericLinks](#schemagenericlinks)|false|none|none|
